Card effects are displayed in chat
abilities.overview:
On use, the player drops their weapon to draw a Tarot card, granting a random temporary effect and gaining 50 overhealth for 1.75 seconds. The various effects and their chances to be drawn are listed below. Pulling the same card before its effect is over resets the timer. Drawing a card takes ~1.6 seconds, during which only Handsfree actions can be performed, including kicking and climbing. An ability charge is depleted at the end of the drawing animation, and each charge has a cooldown of 8 seconds. The cooldown is not interrupted by drawing a card, and 12 Arcana does not have a duplicate ability penalty.

[Common Cards]
Chariot - 16%

Grants +15% move speed.

Hermit - 16%

Grants +50 maximum health.

Magician - 8%

Immediately teleport to a random enemy.

Moon - 16%

Grants -50% ability cooldowns.

Strength - 16%

Grants +7.5% damage dealt.

[Legendary Cards]
Death - 4%
Reduces the user's max health by 75. Uncleansable.

Fool - 4%
Inflicts Reduced.

Fortune - 4%
Grants 850 overhealth that rapidly decays.

Justice - 4%

Dependent on the amount of kills the user has compared to the highest player except them.
- More than 5 kills: -75% damage dealt.
- Less than 5 kills: +75% damage dealt.
- Else: No effect.

Lover - 4%
Boosts healing received by +50%.

Temperance - 4%
Inflicts Tranquilized for 4 seconds.

Tower - 4%
Grants Enlarged for 6 seconds.
abilities.tips:
- It is common to pair 12 Arcana with Susceptible to maximize effect uptime.
- If paired with Barbaric Roar, activating 12 Arcana then immediately roaring can perform both abilities at the same time, saving a few seconds.
abilities.trivia:
- If an ability has more than half its cooldown remaining when moon is activated, that ability's cooldown will immediately be set to half its original maximum.
- Tower and Fool can stack, similar to Transmorph Raygun.
- If one is pulled while the other is active, they simply negate a stack of the other.
- If a player takes double 12 Arcana and repeatedly pulls moon, they can continuously pull cards without stopping (provided no incapacitating effects are inflicted).
- The probabilities provided here are confirmed based on 2500 individual card pulls.

Antiheal will extended if the victim is healed by another player
abilities.overview:
On use, the user throws a small potion of opaque purple liquid that bursts upon impact with another player or surface, dealing 25 damage with no falloff and inflicting Antiheal for 2 seconds on enemies within a 23 stud radius.

Antiheal decreases healing received and dealt by 65%. It also reduces overhealth gained from Bloxy Cola and Magician's Tophat.

Up to 2 charges can be held at once, taking 9.5 seconds to replenish 1.
abilities.tips:
- Due to the potion's relatively slow travel speed, it can be inconsistent when attempting to use at long range against mobile targets.
- However, because its radius is generous and it explodes on impact, it is among the easier area-of-effect projectiles to hit at closer ranges.
- Antiheal can effectively combat teams that rely on healing, but it is important to remember that many sources of overhealth are not affected by Antiheal, and Atmoblaster X-4: Mending V-1 can negate the effect entirely.
abilities.trivia: - Anti-Heal Potion can be caught by Slingshot's "Thanks!" technique. See here for more information.

abilities.name: Barbaric Roar
effects: Enraged for 10 seconds
abilities.description:
Unleash a barbaric shout of power and rampage on your enemies

Lasts for 10 seconds

Grants overhealth based on 2x your passive health bonus (up to +400 max health) for every nearby enemy

Additionally grants +20% character size and +15% increased move speed
abilities.overview:
On use, the user quickly stops and enters a third person animation, letting out a deep roar. The animation lasts for 1 second. During it, the user is under no-move condition, preventing most action inputs.

Within 0.8 seconds of the animation, the user gains Enraged for 10 seconds and overhealth dependent on the number of enemies in a 43-stud radius (not requiring line of sight) and their max health bonus. While under the effects of Enraged, the affected player's character size is increased by 15% and gains 15% increased movement speed. The overhealth granted is double the user current max health bonus per enemy in range. Up to 400 total health can be granted.

The cooldown begins once the user loses all of the overhealth gained from the effect or when Enraged ends, lasting for 10 seconds. While under the effects of Enraged that was self granted, the user cannot use the ability.
abilities.tips:
- The Arcana: Hermit effect can allow weapons with -25 max health penalties to gain overhealth.
- Overhealth per enemy can add up fast in a team fight, though 1.8 seconds is more than enough time to get picked off as a sitting target. Try to create opportunities rather than relying on the overhealth to survive.
- Barring the Fists weapon, this ability does not directly increase damage. However, melee weapons may find the extra size useful in hitting enemies or blocking attacks.
- Many abilities, such as Barrier Shield, also increase in size with the player.
abilities.trivia:
- If the user manages to get 400 or more max health (via Scarlet Aeonia), Barbaric Roar does not grant any overhealth.
- Though the icon depicts a bear, the roar itself appears to be composed of several distinct sounds, most of which do not resemble actual animal calls.

abilities.name: Barrier Shield
abilities.description:
Drop your weapon to raise a massive shield at the cost of mana

Blocks enemy projectiles

Uses mana when damaged

Shield health is increased based on max health

After the company developing Respawn beacons was sold off, the new manager opted to develop ways to *prevent* death than to 'keep allowing Robloxians to live dangerously.' This model focuses Atmo energy on a larger scale.
abilities.overview:
Block enemies and their projectiles using an oversized shield.

On use, the user drops their weapon, enters third person, and equips a large translucent shield that acts as a wall for enemies, blocking projectiles at the cost of mana. Holding the shield drains Mana per second and slows the user by 40%. Handsfree and most movement abilities can be used while holding the shield. Kicking and climbing force the player to drop the shield. It is 26 studs wide and 14 studs tall, and scales proportionally with player size modifiers. The shield can be tilted up and down at a 45° angle.

The shield is considered a forcefield and its health depends on the user's maximum health, including overhealth.
- For max health of 250 and below, the shield's max health equals the user's max health.
- For 251 and above, the shield's health is double the user's health, capping at 600 shield health.
Because this value can change dynamically but the player's current mana does not, it can be useful to think of the shield's health in terms of damage per mana (e.g., 600 shield health means 6 damage = 1 ). Passive mana drain rate and mana recovery are unaffected. For every nearby ally Barrier Shield active, the user's barrier takes +75% increased damage. Additionally, at or lower, the shield visually becomes cracked and 25% of incoming damage dealt to the shield is dealt to the user.

Enemy projectiles are blocked by both sides of the shield, though enemies themselves can pass through the back unimpeded. Because the shield is treated as a wall, enemies can climb over it and homing projectiles ignore players hiding behind it.

After being dropped, Barrier Shield goes on cooldown for 1.75 seconds.
abilities.tips:
- It is typically recommended to equip a weapon that provides a max health of 275 or more, because the boost in shield health that occurs after 250 doubles its efficiency.
- Pushing enemies is inconsistent. Moving sideways is less likely to allow enemies to pass through.
- Tilting the shield downwards can help prevent enemies from climbing over it.
- The shield is not active until the equipping animation is finished, allowing projectiles to seemingly pass straight through it for a brief period.
- Allies behind the shield are protected from blasts and explosions on the other side, though lingering effects such as Poison Mist and Sacrificial Censer's vapors can still affect both the user and their allies from the far side.
abilities.trivia: - Certain weapons and abilities deal more damage/mana than usual, such as Epicsauce, which damages mana by ~66% more than the actual damage it deals.

Slowly pull in an enemy to drain their life force

Reach out and grab an enemy, holding them still and slowly reel them in while draining the target's action points
abilities.overview:
On use, the user fires out a black hand projectile. Upon hitting an enemy, it halts the target's movement and applies Black Hand for 1.5 seconds.

Players under Black Hand are horizontally dragged towards the inflicting user, with the pull strength being dependent on the target's distance away from the user.
- Targets that are 80 or more studs away experience maximum pull strength.
- Targets within 16 studs are unaffected entirely.

Black Hand additionally drains 20 Action Points per second and affects most movement abilities/actions.
- Dash I, Dash II, Rejuvenating Dash, Super Jump, and Chakram's dashes have reduced effectiveness.
- Flight cannot be held.
- Backflight and Sprint are fail casted.
- Icarus and Skateboard's Secondary Fire are disabled.

The cooldown begins after 3 seconds after landing, lasting for 7 seconds. If no targets were hit, it instead goes on cooldown for 1.5 seconds.
abilities.trivia: - Players with Susceptible are affected by the increased duration, however visually the Black Hand disappears after 1.5 seconds.

abilities.name: Call of Valhalla
effects: Enraged for 5 seconds to self and allies
Lifesteal for 4 seconds to enemies
abilities.description:
Unleash a powerful war cry upon your enemies

Inflicts heavy damage and Lifesteal for 4 seconds to enemies within range while granting Enraged (+15% increased move speed) to self and nearby allies for 5 seconds

Additionally grants 25 overhealth to self and 15 overhealth to nearby allies for every nearby enemy (up to +400)
abilities.overview:
While Berserker's Greatsword is equipped, Barbaric Roar is altered to become Call of Valhalla.

On use, the user quickly stops and enters a third person animation, letting out a deep roar. The animation lasts for 1 second. During it, the user cannot input any actions, however can freely look around in the third-person view.

Within 0.8 seconds of the animation, the user begins dealing 10 ticks of damage to enemies within a 35-stud radius around the user. The ticks have a base damage of 5, dealing down to 50% less damage the farther the target is away from the user. Each tick also inflicts Lifesteal for 4 seconds, refreshing the duration when reapplied.

Additionally, the user and allies within 45 studs gain Enraged for 5 seconds. The user and allies gain 25 and 15 additional overhealth for each enemy within a 45-stud radius. Gained overhealth cannot exceed 400 max health and is removed when Enraged ends. While under the effects of Enraged, the affected player gains 15% increased movement speed.

The cooldown begins once the user loses all of the overhealth gained from the effect or when Enraged ends, lasting for 10 seconds. While under the effects of Enraged, the user cannot use the ability.
abilities.trivia: - Call of Valhalla is the first altered ability to feature a different icon from it's original ability.

abilities.name: Chezburger
effects: Grants Heavy for 5s
abilities.description:
Quickly heal up at the cost of becoming heavier!

Eat a burger to restore 75 health at the cost of receiving Heavy for 5 seconds

-15% move speed for every stack of Heavy
abilities.overview:
On use, the user eats a Chezburger, healing 75 health and inflicting Heavy on themself for 5 seconds. When eating another Chezburger while the user still has Heavy, the effect stacks and resets the timer.

Heavy reduces user's movement speed and jump height by 15% multiplicatively per stacks, meaning that 3 stacks reduces the user's speed to 0.85^3 = 61%, rather than 1 - 0.15*3 = 55%. There is a limit of 12 stacks, reducing the user's speed by 85.8%.

It takes 0.6 seconds to eat one Chezburger and 1.25 second cooldown between each use. The health is regained over a short period. While eating, the player can only use Handsfree actions.

Up to 4 charges are held at once, taking 5.5 seconds to replenish one.
abilities.tips:
- Chezburger tends to be most effective with slow and/or bulky loadouts, and is most often paired with Rotary Chaingun.
- The Impervious perk can cut the debuff timer in half, though it is generally more convenient to create a game plan around being slow, such as using Jetpack to avoid normal movement entirely.
- It takes 33 seconds to regain all charges, which makes Swiftcast an effective choice for extended fights.
abilities.trivia: - Though the ability has 4 charges, the deepening of the accompanying sound effect ("Mmm, Chezburger") maxes out at 3 stacks.

abilities.name: Comet
effects: Cold for 4s
abilities.description:
Hold down to transform into a miniature moon and launch into enemies

Deals up to 75 damage and inflicts Cold for 4 seconds which will slow movement speed by 30%

Additionally grants 150% of your passive health bonus as overhealth
abilities.overview:
On use, the player will halt all actions and transform into an opaque comet, gaining flight and exploding on impact. While holding the ability key for up to 3 seconds, the player will fly in the direction they are facing, accelerating up to 60 studs/s over the first 2 seconds. While in the comet, the player enters 3rd person and movement cannot be stopped. Upon ending, releasing the key early, or contacting an enemy or construct the comet will burst in a 15 stud radius, dealing 50 damage and inflicting Cold for 4 seconds, slowing the target by 30% and dealing an additional 15 damage over the duration. Additionally, upon use the player gains 150% of their passive health bonus as overhealth, up to 100. This means that every 25 max health above 200 (excluding bonus health from team-based gamemodes) will provide 37.5 overhealth. Health penalties have no effect.

There is a minimum cast time of 1 second, even if the ability key is released immediately. On impact, the player bounces backwards 16 studs and cannot perform actions for 0.3 seconds. The cooldown begins when the ability ends, lasting for 6 seconds regardless of flight time.
abilities.tips:
- Only weapons with a positive health bonus will gain overhealth.
- Bulkier weapons, such as Fists, Dual Rocket Launchers, or Ban Hammer, will gain the biggest benefit.
- Due to the initial acceleration, you are an easy target for the first second of use. Beware when under fire, especially if your weapon does not provide a health bonus.
- Do not underestimate the blast radius. Ending the ability early when an enemy is nearby will still deal the full damage.
- It can be beneficial to bring a dash to close the recoil distance on impact.
- Watch out for constructs, as the comet hitbox is deceptively large and may trigger on nearby windows or barrels.
abilities.trivia:
- The ability is based off a sorcery spell from the game Elden Ring, Rennala's Full Moon
- Damage from Cold ignores overhealth, which can kill the player through shielding in niche scenarios.

abilities.name: Dash I
abilities.description:
Perform a quick dash with a short cooldown

Provides a burst of speed in your current move direction

Has a reduced cooldown when used with weapons in the Melee category
abilities.overview:
A simple ability used to travel distance.

On use, the player gains a short burst of movement in a horizontal direction. While dashing, the user travels 27 studs in the direction they are holding and is able to perform any action except using their second ability for 0.55 seconds. If no direction is held, the dash defaults to the direction the player is facing.

After the animation finishes, the ability goes on cooldown for 5 seconds, or 4 seconds if the player is wielding a Melee weapon, including subcategories.
abilities.tips:
- Dash I travels the farthest out of the 3 dash abilities (I, II, and Rejuvenating) which makes it the best at closing distance.
- Additionally, Dash I decelerates the least at the end of the dash, making it the best for keeping momentum through bhopping
- Due to how the dashes are designed, Dash I gives the greatest speed in the air out of the 3 dash abilities, though there is no difference when grounded.
abilities.trivia:
- Dash I shares its trail effect with Dash II and Rejuvenating Dash.
- The three abilities also have distinct sound effects that can be heard by other players; Dash I produces a gust of wind, Dash II has a sharper, more dramatic gust, and Rejuvenating Dash makes a magical twinkle.

abilities.name: Dual Arm
abilities.description:
Equip a second pistol for extra damage

Fire up to 28 rounds

+50% bullet damage to targets under 50% health

Activate again or use Secondary fire to unequip early

Cooldown is reduced based on unused bullets
abilities.overview:
While Pistol is equipped, Sidearm is altered to become Dual Arm.

On use, the user equips a pistol in each hand. Together they have a capacity of 28 bullets and a firerate of 7.5 rounds per second in steady 2-round bursts. Each bullet deals 10 damage on bodyshots and 15 damage on headshots (10/15), and Pistol's damage bonus is inverted to +50% if the target is currently below half health. While wielding Pistol's Full Auto technique, ammo capacity is increased to 42, firing rate is increased to 15, and each bullet's damage is reduced by 50% (5/7.5). If Dual Arm is equipped for at least 1.4 seconds, the user's primary Pistol is automatically reloaded while unequipped.

While dual wielding, the player can only use Handsfree abilities. De-equipping the Dual Arm with ammo left over refunds a percentage of the cooldown equal to the fraction of bullets remaining (e.g., 50% off with 14/28 remaining), to a minimum of ~0.3 seconds.
abilities.tips:
- The inverted damage bonus allows for an alternative to Pistol's throw for finishing off low-health enemies.
- The negation of Full Auto's recoil can aid in tracking nimble targets.
- Pistol's Chronorelease technique gains the most utility from Dual Arm, as it temporarily allows the user to revert to normal gun mechanics and deal bullet damage to enemies at any health.
abilities.trivia:
- Despite equipping an entirely new pistol, Dual Arm humorously only gains 1 extra ammo capacity over Full Auto.
- While using Full Auto, Dual Arm's ammo capacity first displays as 28 instead of the increased 42 in a visual bug. This persists until a bullet is fired.
- Dual Arm's bullets can be caught by Slingshot's "Thanks!" technique. See here for more information.

abilities.name: Flight
abilities.description:
Sprout wings, giving a quick burst of speed followed by a short duration of free flight

Hold down the ability key to be in free flight

Movement/abilities are disabled during flight

Costs Action Points
abilities.overview:
The most controllable method of free movement.

On use, the player sprouts glowing golden wings, providing an arcing burst of movement followed by slower free flight, both at the cost of Action Points. The initial burst of movement costs 25 Action Points and travels ~44 studs. It also prevents all actions for 0.4s, or about 3/4ths the distance. If the ability key is held, the player will then enter free flight, moving 30 studs/s while draining 20 Action Points per second. Both the initial burst and free flight are independent of movement speed, though being Dazed locks the ability out entirely.

While flying, the user is under no-move condition, preventing most action inputs.

The cooldown begins once the user stops flying, lasting for 6 seconds.
abilities.tips:
- Staff of Life's Primary and Secondary ignores no-move conditions, allowing it to have free control midflight.
- While flying, holding jump or crouch moves you up or down respectively. Conversely, releasing all movement keys will allow you to hover in place.
- Flight can be used similarly to a basic dash due to its variable cooldown. However, remember that it blocks all actions for a short period.
- Due to its relatively slow speed, predictable movement, and high cost, the free flight is best used to reposition rather than for evasion.
- Watch out for long-ranged weapons, as you're often an easy target while flying.
abilities.trivia: - Equinox Blades' legendary skins change the wings to match the design of the swords.

It travels in the direction it was deployed at 30 studs/s for 3 seconds (90 studs total).

abilities.tips:

- Be aware that deploying the shield prevents all but Handsfree actions for a short period.

abilities.name: Grappling Hook
abilities.description:
Hold down the ability key to send out a grappling hook and reel in

Uses action points while reeling in

Release the ability key to cancel
abilities.overview:
A classic momentum-based movement option.

On use, the player fires a three-pronged grappling hook that pulls them towards the first surface struck, draining action points in the process. The ability key must be held, as releasing the key ends the ability early. While attached, the player is swiftly accelerated towards the hook while airborne and slowly pulled in while grounded. Airborne momentum is greatly enhanced towards and around the hook.

Other actions can still be taken while reeling in, including movement abilities. However, due to the way dashes tend to be hard-coded to have deceleration at the end, they typically do not provide additional velocity; on the contrary, they usually halt most momentum.

The grappling hook has a range of 155 studs, though increasing distance from the hook does not increase acceleration. Reeling in drains action points at a rate of 20/second, regardless of speed. Releasing the ability key, running out of action points, coming within 8 studs of the hook, or causing the line to collide with terrain for 0.5 seconds all end the ability early. The grappling hook can stick to any players or constructs, dealing 15 damage if they were an enemy, and pulling the user towards them as if it hit a surface. The victim's momentum is unaffected.

Cooldown is based on how far the player traveled while attached, with one second being added for each 10 studs traveled, up to maximum of 8 seconds. If either the hook fails to reach a surface or the ability key is released before contact, the ability lingers for 0.5 seconds and is then put on a 1.25 second cooldown.
abilities.tips:
- The variable cooldown means that releasing the key early can be effective in maximizing ability uptime.
- Be aware, however, that distance traveled is tracked for 0.5 seconds after releasing the key, potentially putting the ability on a larger cooldown than expected.
- All airborne momentum is enhanced, including vertical. This means that a hook stuck at eye level can still allow the player to jump over moderately-high walls, given enough horizontal distance.
abilities.trivia:
- The hook cannot be caught by Slingshot's "Thanks!" technique, though it stops the grappling hook mid-air, potentially preventing it from reaching a surface.
- Contrary to how they function in most games, grappling hooks are not designed to stick straight into a surface. Instead, they must be thrown around objects or over ledges such that the hook has an edge to grab, before the user applies tension to set the hook for climbing.

abilities.name: Gravity Disruptor
abilities.description:
Throw a gravity device that will send you and other players upwards while sending enemies downwards

Activates upon landing

Grants a small horizontal boost upon exiting

Lasts for 6 seconds
abilities.overview:
On use, throws a gravity disruptor projectile in the camera's direction. The disruptor bounces off walls until sticking onto the ground.

Upon landing, forms a cylindrical force field that is 60 studs high with a 10 stud radius perpendicular to the ground. When entering, different effects will be applied depending on if they're an ally or an enemy.

- When the user or allies enter and hold JUMP, their vertical velocity is set to a static 25 S/PS. Upon exiting, they are boosted horizontally with a force of 65 and are not be able to re-enter and receive the effects until 3 seconds after they had exited. (Cooldown shared between all gravity disruptors)
- When enemies enter, their vertical velocity is set to a static -25 S/PS.

The gravity disruptor has 50 health, has a lifetime of 6 seconds and is considered a non-humanoid construct.

Shortly after being thrown, the cooldown begins, lasting for 6 seconds.
abilities.tips:
- Players can remain airborne in the Gravity Disruptor by alternating between rising and falling.
- Gravity Disruptor can be used to hard counter Ban Hammer: Grand Slam, resetting it's downward momentum and giving the user an opportunity to escape the radius of their slam.
- When paired with Sacrificial Censer, it can prevent enemies from jumping out of it's ritual.

abilities.name: Healing Orb
abilities.description:
Project a healing barrier over an ally while healing anyone within

Hold down the ability button to select an ally within range

While active, the ability can be used repeatedly to relocate the shield

200 shield health

No longer heals constructs or owned minions.
abilities.overview:
When held, enters a targeting system which can select allied players or minions within a 90-stud radius.

On release on a valid target, the user forms 10-stud radius semispherical barrier around the target. The barrier remains stationary. Allied players within ~13 studs of the shield's origin heal for 50 health per second (no longer heals constructs or owned minions). While the barrier is active, the user can recast it on another ally, having a 0.5 second cooldown between each recast. Recasting does not heal the barrier and retains the same health prior to relocating.

The shield is considered a forcefield and has 200 health. It does not naturally expire however it does get destroyed when the user dies.

When the shield breaks, the cooldown begins, lasting for 4.5 seconds. There is a double equip penalty and the user cannot have more than 1 barrier active at a time.
abilities.tips:
- The shield heals all allies even if they were not the original target, keeping it up in general can benefit the team greatly.
- Unlike other forcefields, enemies are able to walk through healing orb's barrier.
- Users should not expect the Healing Orb to fully protect allies from melee based weapons.
- Both Ban Hammer and Judgement Blade deal increased damage to forcefields.
- Judgement Blade is most effective, capable of breaking the shield at any stage and dealing damage to enemies standing behind it.
abilities.trivia: - Healing Orb's barrier is the only forcefield which enemies can freely pass through.

abilities.name: Healing Potion
effects: 50% move speed and +25% damage taken while drinking, debuff immunity for 3 seconds after
abilities.description:
Heal 100% of HP and cleanse debuffs

Take a 2 second break to chug a healing potion

Heals a large amount of HP and grants debuff immunity for 3 seconds

+25% damage taken while drinking
abilities.overview:
"This is pretty much the best healing potion in any videogame ever." - Roblox

On use, the player equips, drinks, then discards a health potion over the course of 2 seconds, healing the user for 100% of their maximum HP over 1.5s. Healing time is independent of the amount of healing received.

While drinking, the user is slowed by 50%, takes 25% more damage, and the healing effect starts 1.1 seconds into the animation.
abilities.tips:
- Healing potion is one of a few methods of healing that is proportional to the player's maximum health, making it more effective when using bulkier weapons.
- Climbing is possible while drinking; use this to escape if cornered or to save time that would be otherwise wasted.
- Kicking is also possible in a pinch.
- Using the potion before engaging for the debuff immunity is a potential strategy to counter weapons that rely on inflicting debuffs, such as Katana or Sacrificial Censer.
abilities.trivia: - Debuff immunity can cause unintended interactions with certain effects, such as with Black Hand, where the hand remains at the location where it hit the immune target.

abilities.name: Healing Screen
effects: Grants Heal Boost to allies for 3 seconds.
abilities.description:
Send out a wall of healing energy to apply a healing boost to allies

Quickly heals 45 health before boosting incoming healing from all sources by +30% for 3 seconds.
abilities.overview:
On use, the user deploys a translucent green rectangular screen that travels forward to both heal and apply Heal Boost to allies that pass through it.

The screen travels at 50 studs per seconds and lasts for 3 seconds, having an effective range of 150 studs. The initial screen size is 18 studs wide by 12 studs tall and grows up to 2.5x bigger over it's life time.

Allies that pass through the screen immediately heal for 15 health and gain 30 more health over 3 seconds. They are also inflicted with Heal Boost, increasing healing from all sources by 30% for 4 seconds (including self-healing).

While traveling, the screen will pass through any obstacles that do not fully obscure it; the screen will despawn if it is entirely encapsulated in the terrain.

The cooldown begins shortly after use, lasting for 8 seconds.
abilities.tips:
- Both external and self-healing are affected by Heal Boost, but overhealth is not. This makes healing screen more effective on healing supports, like Staff of Life, than overhealth supports, like Bloxy Cola and Magician's Tophat.
- However, because self-healing is also increased, Heal Boost is the only effective method of granting healing to Equinox Blades and Epicsauce due to their external healing penalties.
- Healing Screen can be used in support-heavy teams to temporarily combat the multiple support healing penalty.
- Because it is a status effect, Heal Boost can be used to increase the survivability of allies using Susceptible.
abilities.trivia:
- Heal Boost shares the arrowhead effect of its aura with that of Bloxy Cola's buff.
- Because it is deployed at full size, healing screen can seemingly pass through solid walls upon deploying if the user is close enough to a wall or ceiling such that the screen extends outside the room.
- When deployed vertically, the screen defaults to a north–south wide-axis orientation.

abilities.name: Heartthrob

stats.damage: 30% of current health as self damage

abilities.description:
Dote an ally to trade your health for a burst of healing

Sacrifice 30% of your current health to heal an ally for double the amount sacrificed
abilities.overview:
Transfer your life force to an ally by blowing them a kiss.

Upon use, the player blows a kiss to a damaged ally in the form of a translucent pink heart that heals the target. The user takes 30% of their current health in damage (unmitigated by resistances and overhealth) and the ally is healed for twice that amount.

The ability key can be held to target a single damaged ally within 75 studs. It cannot target through walls. There is a 0.3 second wind up before the healing occurs, and the player is unable to take any actions besides basic movement for a total 0.6 seconds of animation. Although a heart effect flies between the user and the target, the healing itself is effectively instant after the wind up.
abilities.tips:
- Heartthrob is one of the largest burst-healing effects in the game outside of remixes, though it must be used somewhat sparingly. Plan accordingly.
- Healing output is greatly decreased when taking damage in a fight. Try to stay on the back lines or behind cover.
- When creating strategies it is important to remember that overhealth is ignored. Overhealth-providing weapons and abilities, such as Bloxy Cola, require additional setup to capitalize on this ability.
abilities.trivia: - When using the perk Abundance, an ally with full health cannot be targeted even though they can be overhealed.

- Being able to redirect velocity, Hop is commonly paired with weapons or abilities that provide great horizontal mobility, such as Dual Rocket Launchers, Skateboard, and Grappling Hook.
- Horizontal redirection can only apply while mid air. When activated on the group, Hop acts as a slightly higher jump.
- Using Hop with other vertical velocity boosting effects, such as Super Jump or Dual Rocket Launchers, can greatly increase height gain due the upward force being additive.
abilities.trivia:
- Hop uses the same green visual effect as Super Jump, a similar ability that also provides vertical momentum.
- Unlike Super Jump, when double equipping Hop, the user can use both copies in succession.

stats.charges: 1, 2 while using Melee or Support weapons

meta.charges: 1, 2 while using Melee or Support weapons

abilities.description:
Rocket powered leg attachments that allow you to target an enemy or ally and fly to their position

Hold down to select a target and release to fly

Can be cancelled by pressing the ability button again

or end with a boost by pressing Jump or Crouch
abilities.overview:
Icarus is a movement ability that allows the user to fly to enemies or allies.

When held, activates a targeting system on players or humanoid constructs. When released on a valid target, the user quickly flies towards them at a rate of 55 studs per seconds. While midflight, the user can cancel their flight by using the ability again, pressing JUMP, or pressing CROUCH. Reusing the ability causes the user to quickly halt their velocity, JUMP causes them to retain their current velocity, and CROUCH causes them to halt their horizontal velocity and gain vertical velocity.

Icarus holds up to 2 charges while using weapons from the Melee or Support categories, holding 1 charge normally. The cooldown begins after exiting flight, lasting for 7.5 seconds.
abilities.tips:
- Utilizing Icarus's flight cancel function is integral to using the ability effectively.
- The direction your velocity gets redirected with a JUMP cancel depends on the direction you're facing.

abilities.name: Javelin Throw
effects: Applies knockback
abilities.description:
Throw a javelin and knock enemies away

Deals 65 damage and knocks enemies away (no longer inflicts Dazed)
abilities.overview:
On use, the player equips a large throwing javelin that can be thrown by pressing primary fire. Upon hitting a target, it deals 65 damage and inflicts knockback while canceling the target's current velocity. The Javelin has a projectile size of 3.25 studs, flies in a notably straight and fast trajectory, travelling ~170 studs when thrown horizontally.

While equipped, only Handsfree abilities can be used. Pressing the ability button again de-equips the javelin and puts it on a 0.3 second cooldown.

The cooldown begins after being thrown, lasting for 5.5 seconds.
abilities.tips:
- The javelin's high speed and shallow arc allows it to be thrown directly at opponents; In many scenarios, there is no need to account for gravity and minimal need to lead the target.
- Though they may be harder to hit, Dazing airborne enemies will often knock them to the ground by temporarily disabling their flight.
- It takes ~0.2 seconds to equip and ~0.25 seconds to throw the javelin. Make sure to account for this delay in a close-quarters fight.
abilities.trivia:
- Due to its high velocity, the javelin can be thrown significantly farther than the width of most maps. Humorously, if thrown at more than a slight angle above any surface, the javelin will likely remain airborne long enough to despawn before it has the chance to deal any damage.
- Contrary to its name, the model's design—with its pronounced head and wings—appears to be based on Boar Spear or similar hunting weapon, rather than the typical sleek, headless design of throwing javelins.
- Javelin Throw can be caught by Slingshot's "Thanks!" technique. See here for more information.

abilities.name: Jetpack

meta.reference: US Military Top Secret Experimental Jetpack

abilities.description:
Hover and move quickly at the cost of Action Points

Additionally can be activated by pressing Jump
abilities.overview:
When used, the user permanently equips a plane-like jetpack on their back, allowing them to hover by holding the ability or jump keys at the cost of Action Points. Horizontal flight top speed is 32.5 SPS (studs per second), vertical top speed is 20 SPS, and flight always costs Action Points. Flight speed is unaffected by movement speed.

Vertical speed is inversely proportional to horizontal speed, meaning that if the player is moving at 24 studs/s horizontally, they will be rising at 2.5 studs/s vertically. This is most noticeable when turning repeatedly. Additionally, the player must accelerate before they reach top speed. This acceleration is somewhat fast, where turning 180° at full speed only takes ~1 second to reach top speed again. Being Dazed prevents flight entirely.
abilities.tips:
- A small amount of AP is consumed when the ability is activated, meaning that feathering the jetpack does not provide a significant benefit to AP consumption.
- Compared to Flight, jetpack can provide more utility, as it does not lock the player out of performing other actions; though Flight allows for more versatility in its movement due to its more precise control.
- Because flight speed is independent of movement speed, combining jetpack with slower loadouts—such as with Rotary Chaingun—can mitigate most speed penalties.
abilities.trivia:
- Jetpack has the lowest cooldown in the game at 0 seconds.
- When the player first spawns in, the model does not appear on their back until it is used, though afterwards it persists until the player dies.
- The in-game model was actually stolen from the US government's top secret experiments. At least, that's what the name claims.

abilities.name: Life Tether
abilities.description:
Tether onto a teammate to cover and absorb 50% of their incoming damage (no longer grants healing over time)

Consumes mana while active

Absorbs 50% of your tethered ally's damage

-40% healing received to tether ally while covered
abilities.overview:
A long range method of sharing the burden of an ally.

Upon use, creates a translucent barrier around an ally, a shimmering essence around the user, and a connection flowing from the ally to the user that signifies the bond between them. While the tether is active, the user receives 50% of the damage taken by the ally, (no longer grants healing over time), and the ally receives a -40% penalty to external sources of healing. Additionally, the user's mana is drained by 8 per second, unaffected by damage taken. The effect ends when the user either runs out of mana or presses the ability key again.

The ability has a targeting range of ~120 studs and cannot target through walls. However, after the tether is formed it persists through walls and at any distance.
abilities.tips:
- The user can be killed by tether damage.
- Damage resistance reduces the tether damage received by the user.
- Status effects are not transferred to the user.
- Due to its high mana drain, the tether can only last for 6 seconds on its own. Pairing with a source of mana gain can improve overall uptime.
- The cooldown is extremely short, so dropping and restarting the tether can help minimize unnecessary mana drain.
- Similarly, swapping between teammates is simple and can be effective in larger fights.
- Remember that the visual effect for the user and their ally is different.
abilities.trivia: - When dividing an odd number, the upper half goes to the user.

abilities.description:
Halt a victim's momentum by hurling a charged lightning spear at your opponents at the cost of mana

abilities.overview:
On use, wields a lightning spear which is thrown automatically after 0.5 seconds, requiring in order to be used. The ability can be held for an extra 0.5 seconds to charge it and can be released early. While charging the user's movement speed is decreased by 45%. The spear has a projectile size of 4 studs, travels at 240 studs per second and homes onto enemies that are 40 studs off the ground (and are considered ungrounded) or moving faster than 50 studs per second.

The spear explodes upon impact, halting movement, dealing 45 damage and inflicting Dazed for 0.8 seconds in a 8-stud radius. The user is susceptible to the explosion's effects if in range. When fully charged, the spear deals 75 damage on direct hits and explodes in a 16-stud radius instead also being capable of destroying terrain. If the target is above 40 studs off the ground, the direct damage is increased by 50%, dealing 67.5 for uncharged and 112.5 charged hits. If the user is also more than 40 studs off the ground, then the damage is not increased.

Additionally, the spear can wake up allies under the effects of Tranquilized.

After being thrown, consumes up to and goes on cooldown for 0.4 seconds.

Enemies that the ability will lock onto are highlighted.
abilities.tips:

abilities.name: Lockout Curse
effects: Lockout on enemies within range
abilities.description:
Prevent enemies from using their abilities

Throw a cursed box that will inflict Lockout onto all enemies within range

Lasts for up to 3.5 seconds
abilities.overview:
On use, the user throws a small black box covered in glowing red and white symbols to create a spherical red zone upon impact or upon using the ability key again. The zone lasts for 3.5 seconds and enemies within a 25-stud radius are wrapped in translucent red chains and inflicted with Lockout until either they exit the radius or until the zone disappears upon which the effect lingers for an additional 1.2 seconds.

Lockout prevents affected players from activating their abilities and remix. Certain channeled abilities will be canceled upon infliction. Weapon Secondary Fires are unaffected.

The lockout box itself is considered a non-humanoid construct and has 50 health.

The cooldown begins when the lockout box is deployed, lasting for 8 seconds.
abilities.tips:
- Lockout effectively counters players that rely on abilities for consistent support, such as a defensive team using Barrier Shield for cover.
- Do not underestimate the visual noise this effect creates. Placing the zone in the middle of a chaotic battle can briefly confuse unprepared players.
- Watch out for enemy teams that have a lot of area-of-effect weapons, such as Lightning Wand or Grenade Launcher. Blast damage can easily destroy the box, as it only has enough health to survive around two attacks from most weapons.
abilities.trivia: - Lockout Curse can be caught by Slingshot's "Thanks!" technique. See here for more information.

abilities.name: Megawatt Fencing
effects: Inflicts Dazed for 2 seconds
abilities.description:
Set up electric fences that daze and reveal enemies

Throw electric fence nodes to set up

Enemies passing through are revealed through walls and dazed for 2 seconds
abilities.overview:
When used, the user throws a disk-like fencing node which upon contact with a surface, deploys a futuristic fence post in 0.65 seconds. This fence post forms electrical fences with other nodes within line of sight placed by either the user or their ally in a 80-stud radius from itself. The node itself can be placed on an solid surface with any orientation, building the fence perpendicular to the surface.

When an enemy player walks through formed electric fences, they take 65 damage and receive both Dazed and Highlighted for 2 seconds. The electric fencing does not deal damage to targets affected by Dazed but does reapply the effect, refreshing the duration.

Up to 6 nodes can be active at once by the user, destroying the oldest node when attempting to place the 7th. Each node is considered a non-humanoid construct and has 25 health. The hitbox is only on the base/node of the fence post and does not take damage from area attacks or explosions. Nodes which form the electric fence take damage upon shocking enemies, being destroyed after 4 shocks.

Up to 4 charges are held at once, taking 4.5 seconds to replenish one. It has a double equip penalty with itself.
abilities.tips:
- An alternate way to destroy large groups of fences can be the use of piercing attacks such as Chakrams's Primary Fire or Magician's Tophat's Secondary Fire.
- Throwing a node prevents the use of other abilities and attacks for 0.5 seconds (except for kicking). It can be possible to catch opponents off guard by throwing nodes in combat, though make sure to create time before attempting to set up a network.
- 65 damage is not trivial. If dealing damage is the goal, make sure to space the nodes such that the Dazed effect can wear off between triggers.
abilities.trivia:
- Contrary to the description, the electric fence inflicts Dazed for 2 seconds, rather than the 2.5 seconds stated by the description. Additionally, horizontal or upside down posts are somewhat inconsistent and may not always connect to posts of other orientations, especially between normal and upside down.
- Fence posts of different orientations may occasionally connect through walls, though this application is inconsistent and has limited practical use.
- The nodes can be caught by Slingshot's "Thanks!" technique. A node will be fired at high velocity instead of a pellet, ignoring enemies and creating a fence post upon hitting a surface.
- This node counts towards the player's 6 node limit.

abilities.name: Minnow Mage
abilities.description:
Unleash a school of exploding magic minnows to deal damage over time

Send out a portal and summon a school of minnows to damage and slow enemies in its path

An easy and simple spell, said to have been in ancient times when magic was first written. The inhabitants of the Astral Isles say it's likely to be inspired by the schools of fish around the isle.
abilities.overview:
On use, the user temporarily drops their weapon, creating a portal that summons a school of minnows that damage enemies in a cylindrical area lasting for up to 3.5 seconds. The school has a range of up to 60 studs and is 10 studs in diameter. Enemies in range take 70 damage per second and have their movement speed reduced by 50%. When the user dies, the portal disappears.

The minnows do not deal damage through walls, and if the center of the cylinder intersects a wall, the entire effect is blocked at that point. Attempts to cast this ability fail when aiming at a solid surface within 5 studs.

The cooldown begins after the portal disappears, lasting for 6 seconds.
abilities.tips:
- Make sure that you are aiming in the direction you intend to damage, because even a small deviation can result in the end of the effect hitting the ground or aiming too high.
- Crouching or jumping can provide more control over the angle and position of the zone.
- 60 studs is deceptively long. This can be useful in getting the last hit on retreating enemies when your weapon has a short range.
- Placing the minnows in doorways or halls/alleys can make it more difficult to avoid.

abilities.name: Personal Barrier
abilities.description:
Throw to deploy a tri-forcefield to block enemies and projectiles

Last for 12 seconds

100 shield health

After the company developing Respawn Beacons was sold off, the new manager opted to develop ways to *prevent* death than to 'keep allowing Robloxians to live dangerously'. This model focuses Atmo energy on a more personal scale.
abilities.overview:
On use, the user throws a gray pyramid that creates a translucent barrier upon landing on a horizontal surface. The barrier has three pentagonal segments connected to form a semi-triangular shape.

Each segment of the shield is considered a forcefield and has 125 health. The base of the personal shield cannot be damage but does not block projectile nor movement. Additionally, only 33% of the damage dealt to the forcefields is considered as damage mitigated.

After being thrown, the cooldown begins lasting for 6 seconds. It has a double equip penalty with itself.
abilities.tips:
- Weaving back and forth through the barrier is an effective strategy in a 1v1 fight, because the enemy must go around or over it instead.
- The barrier protects players from explosions on the opposite side, though it does not block lingering areas-of-effect—such as the Poison Mist ability.
- Use the barrier to block enemy movement through tight spaces like doorways and alleys, though be aware that enemies can climb over it like any other wall.
abilities.trivia:
- Contrary to the description, each barrier segment has 125 health, as opposed to the 100 stated by the in-game description.
- Each segment has the classic Roblox spawn point decal faintly imprinted on it.
- Once placed, the barrier is unaffected by gravity and can potentially float midair.
- Personal Barrier can be caught by Slingshot's "Thanks!" technique. See here for more information.

abilities.name: Prayer of Defense
effects: Prayer: Defense for ∞s
abilities.description:
Quickly make a short prayer on the move to protect self and nearby allies

Decreases the next instance of incoming damage by 90%
abilities.overview:
Team protection from a single impact.

On use, the player enters 3rd person and slows down to quickly chant a protecting prayer, granting Prayer: Defense to themself and every ally within 32 studs—even through walls. This effect has infinite duration and reduces the next instance of damage by 90%, expiring upon taking damage. The effect lingers for 0.2 seconds after expiration. Indirect damage-over-time is reduced but will not clear this effect, providing consistent protection. While protected, players are surrounded by a gray bubble as a visual indicator.

The prayer takes 1.65 seconds to perform, and the effect is applied halfway through the animation. Movement speed is reduced by 40% while praying, and the player cannot perform any action besides moving, though they can jump and climb for the second half of the animation after the effect is granted.

Holds up to 2 charges, replenishing 1 every 7.5 seconds. There is no double equip penalty.
[Interactions]
Prayer: Defense does not expire when blocking damage from the following sources:
- Damage-over-time status effects
- Bleed
- Burning
- Cold
- Poison
- Rot
- Bloxy Radar
- Magician's Tophat's Primary fire
- Soul Cleave's trail
abilities.tips:
- Because the effect is applied through walls, it is possible to support teammates even while retreating or hiding.
- The gray aura is visible even while you are Invisible.
- Prayer: Defense is one of the few effects that can reduce damage from Rot, though it is cleared upon receiving a stack of Rot, meaning that you must escape before using to gain any benefit.
- Remember that the effect does not protect against negative status effects from blocked damage.
abilities.trivia: - Because the color of the prayer circle changes with team affiliation, the only way to determine the difference between this and Prayer of Speed when used by an enemy is through the symbol that is created above the praying player.

A supportive ability capable of providing increased movement speed and ability cooldown reduction to the user and nearby allies.

On activation, the user enters a 3rd person animation for ~1.6 seconds, dropping their weapon and having their movement decreased by 60%. After 0.4 seconds into the animation, the user and allies within a ~33-stud radius of the user are buffed with Prayer: Speed for an infinite duration.

Prayer: Speed increases the affected player's movement speed by 40% and decreases Abilities cooldown by 40%. The effect expires after they take damage from any source. Additionally, players using weapons in the melee category have their maximum speed cap increased by 40%.

Holds up to 2 charges, replenishing 1 every 5 seconds. There is no double equip penalty.

effects: Halves debuffs' duration
abilities.description:
Briefly take a short prayer stance to heal and halve active debuff durations for self and nearby allies

abilities.overview:
On activation, the user enters a 3rd person animation for 1.6 seconds, dropping their weapon and having their movement decreased by 40%. abilities.name: R.A.I.G. Table
abilities.description:
Kick a military grade wooden table into enemies to heavy damage

Quick kick to launch at enemies

Deals up to 90 damage on a direct hit
abilities.overview:
On activation, the user drops a table that can be launched using Quick Kick. The trajectory depends on the user's view angle, which inverses when looking downwards.
- Looking straight forward sends the table 31 studs horizontally in a low arc.
- Looking at a downwards angle extends the horizontal distance up to 48 studs, though looking straight down sends the table straight up ~25 studs.
- Looking at an upwards angle sends the table higher and slightly farther, though as the viewing angle approaches 45° the table angle approaches vertical, also reaching up to ~25 studs.
Upon impact, the table creates 16-stud radius shockwave which deals damage the closer the target is from the center of the shockwave, up to 45 damage and 15 knockback force, down to 12 damage and no knockback. The shockwave can damage the user. After a 0.4 second windup after activation, the table can directly hit enemies, dealing 90 damage and inflicting 30 knockback force.

The table construct is considered non-humanoid, has 100 health, and expires after 6 seconds.

After kicking the table and being grounded, the cooldown begins, lasting for 6 seconds. There is no double equip penalty, however only one table can be active at a time.

Additionally, the user can "ride" the R.A.I.G. table, sending them in the launch trajectory of the table. In order to pull if off, they must stand on top of the table before kicking it.
abilities.tips:
- The table can be immediately mounted by walking forward while placing. However, this can be inconsistent, especially with non-standard character sizes. Looking downwards greatly increases the consistency of mounting, though smaller sizes must always jump.
- Watch out for fall damage. Angelic Descent can mitigate this issue.
- Falling from max fling height deals 75 damage.
- Pairing with Hop provides great control over the momentum, while Dash II allows for more precise control of higher arcs.
- Beware that if the table impacts a surface or enemy while you're still in the blast radius your flinging momentum will be cancelled.
- Most players use R.A.I.G. Table for the mobility, though do not underestimate its damage and knockback either.
abilities.trivia:
- The shockwave effects are affected by Ban Hammer's Toybox Mallets skins.
- Allies can also be flung with the table like the user.
- Enemies can as well, though the knockback of the table breaking tends to override most of the momentum.
- R.A.I.G. Table is third place for highest damage in a single hit from an ability, right behind Judgement Blade (120) and Time Bomb (100).

abilities.name: Ravenous Maul
abilities.description:
Lunge and grab an enemy to hungrily rip at their neck with your teeth

Hold down to grip onto players

Heal for 100% of bite damage dealt

Can be released early or interrupted by being Quick Kicked
abilities.overview:
On use, the player enters third person and quickly lunges 37 studs over 0.8 seconds in the direction of their crosshair, latching onto and biting into the neck of the first target hit. When held, the user continues to biting into the target, dealing ~66 damage per second and inflicting slight knockback with each tick.

While mauling, the user's turn speed is decreased by 40% and the target's Quick Kick cooldown is decreased by 66%. The maul can be held for indefinitely, however releasing the ability key, getting Quick Kicked by enemies, or receiving knockback effects will kick the user off the target, causing them to flip backwards 20 studs. While lunging, the user is affected by gravity and cannot take any other actions over the course of it except for looking around.

Ravenous Maul holds up to 2 charges and takes 8 seconds to recharge one.
abilities.tips:
- It is a common strategy to use Ravenous Maul with weapons that have a reason to be in the enemy's face, such as Chakrams and Epicsauce, or weapons that inherently have downtime in their damage output, such as Magician's Tophat.
- Certain weapons are more dangerous targets than others: Equinox Blades players will happily Lightspeed to both outdamage and outheal the maul, and Shotgun and Superball are more than grateful to have an easy target from the animation locking upon being kicked.
abilities.trivia:
- Two players may maul each other at the same time, and there seems to be no limit to how long a maul can last.
- The sounds that play upon lunging are produced by creatures known as "Headcrabs" originally from the game Half Life, where they perform a similar function by lunging at and tearing into the player.

abilities.name: Regenerate
effects: Grants Regen for the held duration, then Regen for 3s after releasing
abilities.description:
Heal over time at the cost of mana

Hold down to extend the duration

Lingers for 3 seconds after ending at halved efficiency
abilities.overview:
Self healing at the cost of mana.

When held, the user holds up a ball of swirling green energy, granting themselves Regen while draining 16 Mana per second. While active, the user regains 40 health per second, and can only perform Handsfree actions, including kicking and climbing. After the ability is released, the Regen lingers for 3 seconds, healing at a reduced rate of 20 health per second.

There is an initial delay of ~0.25s before the healing starts, and the ability activates for a minimum duration of 0.6s even if the button is released immediately. Upon ending, it goes on a cooldown of 0.5s.
abilities.tips:
- Regenerate is one of the most versatile methods of self-healing, though it makes you vulnerable while holding.
- When healing while not under direct fire, end the ability early to take full advantage of the lingering effect.
- Combined with good evasion, Regenerate can effectively keep you alive while under fire, though remember that taking damage reduces healing received for a short period.
abilities.trivia: - Regenerate used to have an alteration with Staff of Life called Regeneration.

abilities.name: Rejuvenating Dash
abilities.description:
Perform a quick dash and heal for 20%

Provides a bursts of speed in your current move direction

Kickstarts passive health regeneration on use.
abilities.overview:
On use the user gains a short burst of movement while healing a portion of their health. While dashing, the user travels 22 studs in the direction they are holding and is able to perform any action except using their second ability for 0.55 seconds and heals for up to 20% of their maximum health. If no direction is held, the dash defaults to the direction the player is facing.

After the animation ends, the ability goes on cooldown for 6 seconds.

Kickstarts passive health regeneration on use.
abilities.tips:
- Because of its heal, Rejuvenating Dash provides the most sustain in combat out of the 3 dashes (Dash I, II, and Rejuvenating), though with a higher cooldown it requires more careful engagements and positioning.
- Because the healing is based on maximum health, weapons with a larger health pool receive more benefit from the effect.
- Rejuvenating Dash's ability to kickstart passive regeneration counts being out of combat, and granting the 25 overhealth from Bonus Health.
abilities.trivia:
- Rejuvenating Dash shares its trail effect with Dash I and Dash II, though the healing aura around the user is unique.
- The three abilities also have distinct sound effects that can be heard by other players; Rejuvenating Dash has a healing twinkle, Dash I produces a gust of wind, and Dash II has a sharper, more dramatic gust sound.

abilities.name: Sidearm

meta.caption: "Remember, switching to your pistol is always faster than reloading." - Gaz, 2007

abilities.description:
Quickly swap to a weak pistol for emergencies or to finish off opponents

Fire up to 18 rounds

Activate again or use Secondary fire to unequip early

Cooldown is reduced based on unused bullets
abilities.overview:
Wield a pistol as a backup weapon in a pinch.

On use, the player equips a pistol identical in model to the Pistol primary weapon. It has a firerate of 6.5 rounds per second and a capacity of 18 bullets, though it cannot be reloaded. Body shots deal 12 damage and headshots deal 17 damage.

While equipped, the player can only use Handsfree abilities. De-equipping Sidearm with ammo left over refunds a percentage of the cooldown equal to the fraction of bullets remaining (e.g., 50% off with 9/18 remaining), to a minimum of ~0.3 seconds.
abilities.tips:
- Certain weapons such as Summoner's Codex and Magician's Tophat have periods of limited active damage potential and can make good use of a second weapon.
- Melee users can take Sidearm to deal with the occasional flying target, though a dedicated ranged weapon may be more effective if the enemy team heavily relies on vertical spacing.
abilities.trivia: - Sidearm's bullets can be caught by Slingshot's "Thanks!" technique. See here for more information.

abilities.name: Sprint
abilities.description:
Drop your weapon to sprint at the cost of Action Points

+80% increased move speed while sprinting

Consume more Action Points based on speed
abilities.overview:
The simplest movement option.

On use, the player drops their weapon and runs with a +80% boost to movement speed, draining in the process. While sprinting, only Handsfree abilities can be used.

AP is drained at a rate of ~20.8/second, and this rate increases with higher movement speed. The AP cost increase can be estimated as double the pre-sprint movement speed increase: a +10% speed buff becomes +20% AP drain rate, and +25% speed equates to +50% drain rate. The result is that a higher movement speed provides less total distance traveled before running out of AP. Movement speed decreases cannot be estimated with this formula, though equipping the perk Body: Large causes a ~30% decrease to AP drain rate.
abilities.tips:
- Speed boosts are multiplicative, meaning that stacking weapon speed and sprint makes both more effective.
- Combining Sprint with the perk Body: Small can make for an incredibly slippery target.
- There is half a second of acceleration before hitting top speed, so don't expect to disengage instantly.
- This combined with the slight cooldown prevents feathering the ability to reduce AP cost.
- Airborne acceleration is not affected, though getting a running start can allow the player to jump across large gaps.
abilities.trivia: - When the player is slowed, the sprinting animation is slowed to match, sometimes to humorous effect for larger speed penalties.

abilities.overview:
An area speed boost that dazes enemies.

On use, the player throws a pointy white star-shaped object that bounces three times to create standing sigils that grant allies Starspeed before exploding, attracting enemies and inflicting Dazed. The fragment detonates upon contacting a surface for the third time, and it disappears without detonation if it travels for 3 seconds. - The bounce pattern of the fragment can be manipulated by the throwing angle, where throwing forwards results in a shorter bounce and throwing upwards or downwards results in a higher bounce.

abilities.description:
Throw a dart that will fully tranquilize an enemy

abilities.overview:
A precise method of complete incapacitation.

On use, the player pulls out a small tranquilizer dart that can be thrown using Primary Fire to put an enemy to sleep. On hit, it deals 10 damage and applies the Tranquilized status for 1.25 seconds, putting the affected enemy to sleep in third person and preventing them from performing any actions for the duration. This effect ends early if the enemy takes any damage, and when the effect is over it takes 0.25s for the waking animation to complete before the enemy can act.

The tranquilizer dart is one of the few projectiles to completely ignore gravity, and it flies far enough to have effectively infinite range on all maps. While holding the dart, only Handsfree abilities can be used. The ability key can be pressed again to put the dart away, incurring a cooldown of ~0.3s.

After being thrown, the cooldown begins, lasting for 10 seconds.
abilities.tips:
- The dart flies straight and fast for effectively forever, making it one of the most precise projectiles in the game. Only speed must be taken into account.
- Wait until the target is close enough to you or your allies to take advantage of the effect, because the duration is relatively short.
- Weapons with high burst damage can make great use of the target's complete immobility, such as Slingshot: Fast Firing or General's .45: Quickdraw.
abilities.trivia:
- When thrown across the map, the dart can fly so far off the opposite side as to despawn outside of any player's render distance.
- The dart can be caught by Slingshot's "Thanks!" technique. A tranquilizer dart will be fired instead of a pellet, dealing 10 damage and tranquilizing the target as normal.

abilities.name: Translocator
abilities.description:
Leave behind a teleportation device to return to

Press the ability key to teleport to your translocator

Cooldown is reduced based on teleport distance
abilities.overview:
When activated, the user throws a small disk-shaped glowing device that sticks to the first horizontal surface contacted. When used a second time, the user teleports to the device, cancelling all momentum and gaining invincibility for 0.5 seconds.

The teleportation device is considered a non-humanoid construct and has 50 health. It can be destroyed by the user and their enemies.

After teleporting, the cooldown begins, with the duration being based on teleportation distance: 6 seconds when under 45 studs up to 10 seconds when over 190 studs. When destroyed, it is put on cooldown for 10 seconds.

Translocator does not have a double equip penalty, though the user cannot throw a second device until the first has been used.
abilities.tips:
- Translocator, alongside Portal Pair, is one of the few methods of movement that instantly changes your location. This makes it useful for escaping situations where fast movement might not be enough, such as a Scarlet Aeonia landing on your location.
- Placing the device in covenient locations—such as on a medkit—can be useful, though ensure that it is not placed in an obvious location where your enemies will notice it.
- Conversely, don't spend so much time hiding it that teleporting takes you far enough away to put you out of the fight for longer than respawning would have.
- In a pinch, teleporting early can allow for short range mobility similar to the initial burst of Flight.
- The device does not persist after dying.
abilities.trivia:
- Drifter is triggered when throwing the device, but not when teleporting.
- No matter the angle faced when thrown, the translocator device always points in the cardinal directions.
- The translocator used to be catchable by Slingshot's "Thanks!" technique, taking up 1 slot. The device was fired instead of a pellet, acting as normal, though it was useless even if the Slingshot user had their own Translocator ability.

abilities.name: Trowel
effects: Bleed
abilities.description:
Build a defensive wall for cover or to block off opponents

R to rotate the placement position

Additionally builds barbed wire above walls

Owned walls are see-through up close

175 wall health
abilities.overview:
Instant cover that punishes reckless play.

On use, the user drops their weapon and equips a trowel. While holding the trowel, the wall's placement is displayed, with a max horizontal range of 20 studs and vertical range of 4 studs. Pressing Reload changes the wall between perpendicular and parallel, indicated by the two dots that replace the user's crosshair as well as a slight flick the player performs with the trowel.

Pressing Primary Fire on a valid placement constructs the wall, slowing down the player by around 50% which is visually constructed over a short period, though the hitbox is fully active immediately. Players are lifted on top of the wall when placed underneath them. The wall is 28 stud wide, 12 studs tall, 2 studs thick, and has barbed wire on the top of the trowel that deals 50 damage and inflicts Bleed for 3 seconds, totaling to 80 damage to enemies that touch it. Allied players are able to see through walls when within 12 studs of one.

Walls are considered non-humanoid constructs, have 175 health, and is damageable by both enemies and allies. The user can have up to 6 walls active at a time, destroying the oldest one when attempting to place more, and they last indefinitely until the user dies or until they are destroyed. Additionally, 50% of damage dealt to a wall is dealt to other walls in a 16-stud radius, and 33% of the damage dealt by other players is considered as mitigation.

Up to 3 charges can be held at once, replenishing one every 6 seconds, and there is no double equip penalty.
abilities.tips:
- Placing walls is one of the easiest ways to control enemy movement, especially around doors and halls. However, be aware that you are also blocking your own teammates' movement and abilities.
- Walls clip through terrain, making blocking doorways and oddly shaped structures much easier.
- Due to its instant construction, placing a wall is one of the fastest ways to blocking telegraphed attacks. This even includes powerful Remixes like Scarlet Aeonia and Divine Veil.
- Placing a wall underfoot can also provide extremely fast vertical movement, though if you are moving too fast the wall may be placed beside you instead.
- The barbed wire hitbox is large enough that players can take damage just for jumping around the wall without even climbing it.
- Building a wall under an enemy is guaranteed damage if they get lifted by it.
- Pairing with the improved wall jump from High Climb can allow for tricky and unpredictable movement.
abilities.trivia:
- Walls do not count for damage dealt.
- Trowel had an ability alteration with Minigun that has since been removed: Barricade
- Placing a trowel wall on top of a Translocator will cause the teleporting player to be instantly killed with the death message "[Name] teleported into a wall". Team affiliation of the wall is irrelevant.
- Active walls keep their relative team affiliation if a player is teamswapped, even through death (i.e., walls placed by an enemy-now-friend will still appear red and damage the player).

remixes.name: Aerial Support
effects: Dazed
remixes.description:
Spawn an attack helicopter and equip a deadly sniper rifle

Lasts up to 25 seconds or until the helicopter is destroyed

Helicopter will crash and explode upon impact
remixes.overview:
[Activation]
When activated, the user immediately enters an attack helicopter while quickly rising and equips a Sniper Rifle for 25 seconds. Additionally, pressing the Remix button swaps between the Sniper Rifle and the user's main weapon with a 2 second cooldown between each swap.

Upon entering, disables input for 0.6 seconds.

[Attack Helicopter]
The Attack Helicopter has 800 health and is considered non-humanoid. Both enemies and allies can collide and stand on the helicopter.

Movement controls can be used to fly in any direction, moving around ~50 S/PS. Additionally, the Jump and Crouch key can be used to ascend and descend respectively. The helicopter will gradually match with the direction the user is also facing.

Upon contact with a surface or expiring, the helicopter crashes and explodes, dealing 125 damage and inflicting Dazed to enemies within range, also kicking out and dealing 25 damage to the user. However, it cannot be forced crashed within the first 3 seconds of entering.

Near the end of the duration or under 150 health, the helicopter will begin to descend rapidly. When close to a surface, the helicopter will play a beeping noise.

While the user is riding the Attack Helicopter they will have access to the Sniper Rifle.

[Sniper Rifle]
[Primary]
When held, fires a hitscan bullet with heavy recoil. Each bullet deals 150 damage on bodyshots and 300 damage on headshots. Has a fire rate of 0.8 seconds.

[Secondary]
When held, scopes in, zooming the FOV by 10 times and reducing recoil. Additionally, the Primary Fire's becomes fully accurate.

[Passive]
While equipped, creates a red laser visible to enemies.
remixes.tips:
- This Remix is almost useless in Mad Tech Factory, as it's an entirely enclosed map with no sky to fly whatsoever. The only thing it can do is explode and daze nearby players, which can be somewhat useful, but you're likely better off using more reliable Remixes.
- The player riding the helicopter can still be shot directly. If they are using the Body: Large perk, they are at a big disadvantage, as the feet can clip through the bottom of the helicopter.
- Other players, whether allies or enemies, can collide with and ride in the helicopter.
[Playing]
- Your Sniper Rifle shows a laser towards where you're aiming, meaning players can avoid your line of sight to avoid being shot.
- Remember, you can switch your weapon by pressing the Remix ability again. Use this to your advantage to finish off players with your main weapon if your target is on low health.
- Try not to flash your laser towards enemies for too long, as they'll try to dodge your attacks.
- Before the Remix duration ends, fly towards a group of enemies to daze and deal hefty damage to them.
- Even if you can't get consistent headshots, 150 damage is still a high number and can leave enemies at low health for others to finish or for you to finish off.

[Countering]
- Stay away from the direct line of sight of the Sniper. If you can, focus on the player riding the helicopter to kill them before the helicopter falls and explodes on you.
- You can use Slam Dunk to hinder the rider and lower them greatly.
remixes.trivia:
- The Sniper Rifle used to be a normal weapon which players could use freely.
- The person operating the Helicopter is Mateo
- Aerial Support's sniper shots can be caught by Slingshot's "Thanks!" technique. See here for more information.

remixes.name: Artemis' Bow
effects: Grants free flight temporarily, summons arrow zones which damage enemies and heal allies while bypassing Antiheal's extended duration
remixes.description:
Fly for up to 8 seconds and mark up to 4 areas for damaging enemies and healing allies

Fire up to 4 arrows to create arrow zones that will damage enemies over time and heals allies for double

Arrow zones will last for up to 6 seconds
remixes.overview:
[Activation]
When activated, the user gain Artemis' Bow for up to 8 seconds.

While having the bow equipped, the user is able to move freely in the air, using directional keys to move forward, sideways, or backwards, and Space and CTRL key to ascend or descend respectively.

The user has a horizontal flight speed of ~41.3 studs per second and a vertical flight speed of 22.5 studs per second. Additionally, the flight speed can be increased/decreased from their weapon's passive or status effects.
[Primary]
When held, charges up an arrow, being fully charged after 0.3 seconds.

On release, the arrow is fired, with its velocity being dependent on how long it was charged for. Hitting walls or roofs causes arrows to bounce off them.

When the arrow hits the ground, it summons an arrow zone which damages enemies and heals allies.
- Deals 30 damage per second (5 damage every 1/6th of a second) with the first tick dealing 25 damage.
- Heals 60 health per second (10 health every 1/6 of a second) with the first tick healing 50 health. Additionally does not extend Antiheal's duration.

Arrow zones have a radius of 20 studs, a height of 25 studs, and a lifetime of 6 seconds.

Up to 4 shots can be fired, shortly unequipping the Artemis' Bow after usage.
remixes.tips:
[Playing]
- Firing 2 arrows at the start of activation, then firing 2 more at near the end of the duration can provide longer sustain and allow the user to conserve the free flight for longer.
- This is great for zone based game modes, especially during overtime.
[Countering]
remixes.trivia:
- The free flight's duration is affected by Impervious.
- However, Susceptible does not affect the duration as the free flight cannot exceed the remix's duration.
- Artemis' Bow's arrows can be caught by Slingshot's "Thanks!" technique. See here for more information.
- The sound cue for this remix comes from a short sample of 'Space' from the Terraria official soundtrack.

remixes.name: Blox Card Assist
effects: Inflicts Dazed (Blue), Lockout (Red), or Defense Shred for 6 seconds (Cami).
remixes.description:
Call upon a random character's past experience of war to assist in battle

[COLLAB ITEM]

Brought to you by Blox Cards
remixes.overview:
Using Blox Card Assist calls down Blue, Red, or Cami to assist in combat, each using their own unique attack. When held out, it display the area of effect of the character's attack.

Upon use, the user throws the card at the spot they are looking at up to ~120 studs away.
[Blue]
When summoned, Blue appears wielding dual rocket launchers. After a ~0.9 second start up Blue begins firing rockets, dealing damage to every enemy within a 30 stud radius dealing 35 damage each attack up to 315 total damage.

[Red]
When summoned, Red appears wielding dual crimson katanas. After a ~1.1 second start up time, Red swings both crimsons around dealing 8 damage rapidly to anyone within 25 stud radius of him to deal a total of 112 damage. Each hit inflicts ~2.4 seconds of Lockout to enemies, resetting the duration if they get damaged again.

[Cami]
When summoned, Cami appears wielding a sniper, during her animation she shoots down an airplane dealing 200 damage and killing the pilot (Does not count as actual damage/kill). After a ~4.4 second start up time, the airplane comes crashing down damaging anyone within 50 stud radius of the impact for 150 damage, applying Dazed for ~3.2 seconds and Defense Shred for 6 seconds.
remixes.tips:
- Should be often be used during objective game modes where players are more clumped together. The area of effect usually are big enough to cover most of the point
- Blue most notably dealing massive amounts of damage in a solid radius.
remixes.trivia:
- Dealing a finishing blow with this remix grants the "Blox Cards Assist" badge.
- Apex of Babylon was originally meant to be apart of the card pool, but was removed due to clipping issues.
- The sound cue for this remix comes from a short sample of Rainbow Tylenol by Kitsune^2.
