remixes.name: Bubble Barrier
remixes.description:
Drop a barrier bubble that blocks enemy projectiles

Drop a barrier projector and make a large protective bubble around for 6 seconds that block enemies and projectiles
remixes.overview:
[Activation]
When activated, a projector is dropped from the user's position.

Upon hitting the ground, the projector create a forcefield construct that is a hollow 18-stud radius sphere, which is missing half of its bottom hemisphere. The forcefield's health is dependent on how many other players are in the lobby, having initially 400 health and adding 75 for each person that isn't the user.

Enemies can deal damage to the projector to deal critical damage for weapons that have it.

When the forcefield's health is depleted, it will be removed but the projector remains until its duration ends.

After 6 seconds, both the projector and forcefield expires.
remixes.tips:
[Playing]
- Bubble Barrier can be used to trap enemies using their remixes, notably Bladed Tutu, Scarlet Aeonia, and Stravant's Lightning
- It can also prevent enemies from reaching objectives, notably blocking off Flag carriers in Fishin' For Flags.

[Countering]
- Being around ledges provides an advantage as there is an opening at the bottom.
- Judgement Blade deals +600% increased damage to the Bubble Barrier, dealing a heavy blow to it's health.
- Laser Finger Pointers are able to heal allies inside the Bubble Barrier
- Portal Pair and Portal Gun are able to teleport in and out of the Bubble Barrier, allowing allies to get out or surprise enemies inside.
- When trapped alone inside a Bubble Barrier, General's .45: Try Your Luck's Secondary fire deals damage to the barrier with every bounce, shredding its health.
- Artemis' Bow, Crimson Katana, Blox Cards Assist, and Glare of Medusa are capable of dealing damage through the barrier.

remixes.name: Divine Veil
remixes.description:
Float into the air before unleashing divine energy which will push back nearby enemies and shield nearby allies

Grants +800 overhealth to all allies within range for 8 seconds

Damages all nearby enemies for 30% of their max health
remixes.overview:
When activated, the user enters a third-person animation, disabling actions except for looking around while rising up 7.5 studs into the air. After 1.2 seconds, the user bursts divine energy in a 60-stud radius around them, dealing different effects to enemies and allies.
- Allies in range receive 800 overhealth which decays over 8 seconds.
- Enemies within line of sight and range take 30% of their max health as damage, dealing a minimum of 50 damage.

After 0.8 seconds of releasing the divine energy, the user exits the animation.
Divine Veil costs 1600 build charge (2462 for non-support weapons) and lasts for 9 seconds, after which it can begin recharging again. Dying within 0.5 seconds of activation refunds used charges.
remixes.tips:
[Playing]
- Divine Veil can perfectly counter Subspace Minefield, destroying all trip mines while providing overhealth to the team.
- Additionally, because constructs are not checked for line of sight, Divine Veil can be used behind walls to clear them.
remixes.trivia:
- The sound cue for this remix comes from a short sample of 'Riders Of The Light' from Bayonetta.

[Countering]
- Teddy Trap can prevent Divine Veil from activating when it's thrown during the start-up animation.
- It does not need to kill the user to prevent it.

remixes.description:
Rain missiles on your opponents and daze them

The Primary launches out 8 arcing rockets projectiles with heavy spread which explode in a 20 stud radius upon impact. Additionally, the explosions are capable of terrain destruction and inflicts Dazed for 1 second. Direct hits from the rocket deals 75 damage. Between each use there is a cooldown of around 2 second.

The explosions are capable of damaging the user, however it is reduced by 50% and additionally applies ~10 knockback force.
remixes.tips:

- Always calculate the trajectory of your shot to be able to catch as many enemies as possible in the center of the explosion area

remixes.name: Fae Circle
effects: Grants the user Fae Circle for 10 seconds
remixes.description:
Create a magic circle of life that heals and cleanses you and nearby allies

Heal and prevent debuffs to all allies within range

Doubles ally healing received when below 50% health

Lasts for 10 seconds
remixes.overview:
When activated, the user instantly gains Fae Circle for 10 seconds. (The duration is unaffected by Susceptible and Impervious)

While Fae Circle is active, the user gains a magical circle around them that heals them and allies within a 40-stud radius for 50 health per second while providing debuff immunity. Additionally, when allies are below 50% health, they receive double incoming healing from all sources.

Dying within 1 second of activation refunds the remix.
remixes.tips:
[Playing]
- Staff of Life commonly uses Fae Circle due its healing over time that covers a large radius, providing for Secondary Fire on certain techniques.
- Fae Circle can be used to counter status effect based Weapons and Remixes.
- Weapons include Casting Staff, Summoner's Codex, and Sacrificial Censer.
- Remixes include Eternal Flame and Crimson Katana.

[Countering]
- Fae Circle cannot cleanse Scarlet Aeonia's Rot debuff, allowing the damage over time to nullify or overpower the user's own healing over time.
- Weapons or remixes that deal high burst damage can be effective in taking down the user while Fae Circle is active. Especially when the user is using support weapons with lower health pools.
- Weapon and techniques include Ban Hammer: Grand Slam and Grenade Launcher: Sticky Grenades.
- Sacrificial Censer also deals high burst damage, however successfully sacrificing targets can be difficult due to Fae Circle's cleansing effects.
- Remixes include Hyperlaser Gun, Marble Madness, and Golden Knife.

effects: Reveals enemies and their health to the user and allies within a 75-stud radius from the Satellite Intel
remixes.description:
Deploy a portable satellite dish to grant intel to your team

Reveals footprints/direction/health from enemies within 150 studs to you and your team

Additionally acts as a spawn location similar to an ally even on objective zones

Lasts up to 45 seconds
remixes.overview:
The Satellite Intel is a utility remix which grants the user and their team information about enemies within range.

[Activation]
When activated, the user throws out Satellite construct projectile in the direction they're facing.

When the projectile collides with any surface, it builds a Satellite construct perpendicular to the surface. It can be built on floors, walls, and ceilings.

Once constructed, the Satellite activates immediately, looping a radar sound while it is up. The Satellite reveals the direction, footsteps, and health of every enemy within 75-stud of the construct. The user and allies are able to see the details through walls, however enemies will not be able to see that they're being tracked.

Additionally, the user and their allies can spawn onto of the radar even under objective zones, granting +25 initial overhealth without the increased spawn in time.

The Satellite construct has 100 health and is considered non-humanoid. After 45 seconds of being constructed, it will destroy itself.

The remix requires 750 build cost to use and begins recharging once it is thrown.
remixes.tips:
- The satellite is easily destroyed, so make sure to hide it well. Behind high walls and on ceilings work best.
- Satellite intel works best in team game modes with a fixed point.

remixes.name: Scarlet Aeonia
effects: Applies Rot for 6s
Inflicts Dazed for 1s upon landing
remixes.description:
Burst into a large flower and inflict Rot onto all enemies in range

Receive +400 max health for 8 seconds upon use

Fly up before landing down where you're facing and unleash 25 damage-per-second to enemies within range for 4 seconds

A forbidden magic born from a shared wish between the of the Astral Isles and the servants of the Korblox. With making and unmaking unable to unite, a terrible rot was born.
remixes.overview:
On activation, the user gains 400 max health, enters a 3rd person POV and rises up 30 studs over 2 seconds, sprouting translucent orange petals (Blue when viewed from an ally.) After a short delay, the user begins to fly downwards at ~350 studs/s towards where their camera is angled. The angle they fly at is limited, assuming that 0 degrees is the user looking straight forward, at most the user can fly at a -18.5° angle. Upon landing, the user deals 10 damage and inflicts Dazed for 1 second in a 20-stud radius.

After 3.33 seconds of activation, the flower blooms, dealing an initial 50 damage to enemies and inflicts Rot for 6 seconds every 0.33 seconds over a duration of 4 seconds, effectively applying Rot up to 12 times. The bloom targets enemies in a ~15-stud radius and requires line of sight. Rot is an uncleansable debuff which deals 25 damage per second per stack to the affected player for each stack, maxing out at 8 stacks.

For the first 4.5 seconds of activation, the user cannot use their weapons or abilities. After landing the user may begin to use abilities.
remixes.tips:
[Playing]
- The blooming effect does not require the user to be grounded to activate. This means at a certain distance, the bloom is able to activate shortly upon being in range of enemies providing little to no time to counter the attack.
[Countering]
- Getting behind cover is one of the best ways to avoid the attack as the bloom requires line of sight to inflict Rot
remixes.trivia:
- The maximum health's duration is affected by Susceptible and Impervious.
- Scarlet Aeonia is likely based on the Servant of Rot Incantation from Elden Ring with the same name.
- The sound cue for this remix comes from the soundtrack which plays during the fight with Malenia, Goddess of Rot.

remixes.name: Soul Binding
effects: Trail fully heals minions and applies a life tether between them and the user for 12s, reducing the user's and tethered minions' damage taken by 50% (working both ways). Additionally inflicts Antiheal for 3s and enemies killed within the trail are turned into zombies.
remixes.description:
Cleaving through an owned summon will fully restore their health before attaching a Life Tether to you both for 12 seconds, redirecting 50% of incoming damage to them instead

Marks a lingering trail of Anti-Heal for 3 seconds

Additionally causes enemies to rise from the dead (additional Remix Ability charge and passive regen from attacking zombies)

The Deathwalker are powerful beyond compare; raising the dead by treating souls as if they were clay to be mould. Wielding it too long may make your presence known to the King.
remixes.overview:
While Zombie Staff is equipped, Soul Cleave is altered into Soul Binding.

Soul Binding is an area-of-effect damage remix that can inflict Antiheal. It has a build cost of 1300.

On use, the user enters a third person animation and swings a larger glowing Zombie Staff 6 times forward, leaving a glowing white trail along the staff's path. During the animation, the user cannot use abilities, however can move their camera to change their direction. The trail inflicts Antiheal for 3 seconds, reduce max health by 50 for 5 seconds and deals 60 damage per second to enemies that remain in contact. The trail dissipates uniformly after 6 seconds of activation.

When the user's minions comes in contact with the trail, they are fully healed and become tethered to the user for 12 seconds. While tethered, the user takes -50% incoming damage while the tethered minion takes 50% of the user's incoming damage. Multiple tethers stack multiplicatively, meaning that 2 tethered minions reduces incoming damage by 75%, and each tethered minion takes 25% of the user's incoming damage. Additionally, tethered minions also have 50% damage reduction which stacks when receiving the user's damage. When the user deals damage to themselves, they take reduced damage however tethered minions receive no damage at all.

Additionally, enemies killed while in the trail are turned into zombies. Zombified players are humanoid constructs which have 100 health, deal 25 damage every 0.5 seconds, and inflicts Dazed with every hit. They are also considered neutral, attacking nearby players regardless of team.

After the remix is unequipped, it can begin recharging.
remixes.tips:
[Playing]
- Soul Binding is an incredible source of Antiheal, inflicting it over a large area. This allows it to excel in objective based gamemodes that also have multiple support players on the other team.
- While tethered to 3 Deathwalker Servants, the user's damage reduction is up to 87.5%, allowing the user to rush into fights,
[Countering]
- Prayer of Defense can be used to negate the damage dealt as Prayer: Defense will not be removed when taking damage from the trail.
- However, this does not protect the user from Antiheal and one direct hit can break the shield, leaving them vulnerable.
remixes.trivia:
- Soul Binding is the first altered remix ability.
- Tethering is not limited to Zombie Staff's Deathwalker Servants. Summoner's Codex's Phoenix, Burst Rifle's Rookie, and Sacrificial Censer's clone can be tethered.
- This can be achieved via Mastery Roulette, however it is very impractical to pull off during a match.
- The zombified players are very similar to the ones found in the map Kin. They share the same damage, health, and animations, however Kin zombies inflict more knockback.
- Additionally, Kin zombies are immune to the Soul Cleave trail. This is likely due to the fact that the zombification mechanic used to be present in Kin, when players died on the map, they would have a chance to be revived as a zombie.

remixes.name: Soul Cleave
effects: Inflicts Antiheal for 3s. Enemies killed within the trail are turned into zombies.
remixes.description:
Be lifted by the gift of a Korblox Axe, leaving a trail of lost souls that will prevent enemies from being healed or giving heals

Marks a lingering trail of Anti-Heal for 3 seconds

Additionally causes enemies to rise from the dead (additional Remix Ability charge and passive regen from attacking zombies)

The Deathwalker are powerful beyond compare; raising the dead by treating souls as if they were clay to be mould. Wielding it too long may make your presence known to the King.
remixes.overview:
On use, the user enters a third person animation and swings a large Korblox Axe 6 times forward, leaving a glowing white trail along the axe's path. During the animation, the user cannot use abilities, but can move their camera to change their direction. The trail inflicts Antiheal for 3 seconds, reduce max health by 50 for 5 seconds, and deals 60 damage per second to enemies that remain in contact. The trail dissipates uniformly after 6 seconds of activation.

Enemies killed while in the trail are turned into zombies. Zombified players are humanoid constructs which have 100 health and deal 25 damage every 0.5 seconds. They are also considered neutral, attacking nearby players regardless of team.

After the remix is unequipped, it can begin recharging.
remixes.tips:
[Playing]
- Soul Cleave is an incredible source of Antiheal, inflicting it over a large area. This allows it to excel in objective based gamemodes that also have multiple support players on the other team.
[Countering]
- Prayer of Defense can be used to negate the damage dealt as Prayer: Defense will not be removed when taking damage from the trail.
- However, this does not protect the user from Antiheal and one direct hit can break the shield, leaving them vulnerable.
remixes.trivia:
- Soul Cleave is the first remix ability to be altered by a weapon. This alteration is Soul Binding, while using the weapon Zombie Staff.
- The zombified players are very similar to the ones found in the map Kin. They share the same damage, health, and animations, however Kin zombies inflict more knockback.
- Additionally, Kin zombies are immune to the Soul Cleave trail. This is likely due to the fact that the zombification mechanic used to be present in Kin, when players died on the map, they would have a chance to be revived as a zombie.
- The model is not apart of the Korblox set and is recolored version of Axe of the Divine Flame.

remixes.name: Teddy Trap
remixes.description:
Force someone to equip a teddy bear that explodes upon use

Explodes after 1 second after being hugged and instantly kills the user
remixes.overview:
[Activation]
When activated, equips a throwable Teddy Trap for up to 8 seconds.
[Primary]
On use, throws the Teddy Trap, unequipping it. Upon contact with an enemy, they equip a teddy trap temporarily for 2 seconds. (The duration can be shortened but not extended)

When thrown at a humanoid construct, the Teddy Trap activates immediately, dealing 300 damage to the construct and causing an explosion which deals up to 300 damage to nearby enemies.
[Teddy Trap]
The Teddy Trap overrides the affected player's equipped item, including remixes, which will not be restored when the duration ends. It also forces the player's POV to first person. When equipped, there is a 0.25 second delay before usage.

Using Primary or Secondary fire causes the affected player to hug the teddy which causes it to explode after a one second delay. The explosion deals 1000 damage to the user and can damage nearby players, dealing up 300 damage with heavy falloff. Additionally, the explosion can damage and knockback the user who threw the teddy bear.
remixes.tips:
[Playing]
- Teddy Trap can be effective against multiple weapons, as a majority of them require holding down Primary or Secondary fires to use them well.
- However it does depend on the player who uses that weapon in the end, noting down player's attack patterns can allow you to get better value out of the Teddy Trap.
- Teddy Trap is very useful in cancelling other remixes, with it's low cost compared to most, it's easy to have on the go in the case someone decides to pull one out.
- Bladed Tutu, Stravant's Lightning, Glare of Medusa, Crimson Katana, and Golden Knife rely on the duration of their remix to gain value, so cancelling them is a great way to gain value out of Teddy Trap
- Divine Veil and Scarlet Aeonia are great remixes to cancel with their wind ups.
- Fae Circle and Aerial Support cannot be cancelled entirely, as they retain their remixes ability after Teddy Trap ends in the case they don't explode.

[Countering]
- Teddy Trap is canceled by non-humanoid constructs completely, defensive abilities such as Trowel and Barrier Shield can provide that protection.
- Prayer of Defense grants protection to the explosion damage, reducing its damage down to 100.
- Immunity frames can negate the explosion completely, Translocator and Burst Rifle: Deployable Rookie's Secondary teleport both grant immunity frames on demand.
- The Teddy Bear's equipped duration can be shortened by Impervious, Equinox Blades, and Epicsauce.
- Stacking Impervious with either weapons can reduce the equip time down to 0.5 seconds.
remixes.trivia: - Teddy Trap can be caught by Slingshot's "Thanks!" technique. See here for more information.

perks.name: Ghostwalker
perks.description: When reaching 1 health, turn into a 75 health free-roaming ghost before reviving after surviving for 5 seconds
perks.overview: While equipped, dying causes the user to turn into a ghost, removing all current status effects and gaining Reviving for 5 seconds. While under Reviving, the user becomes a translucent ghost with 75 health, entering 3rd person. While in ghost form, the user cannot be healed, use their weapons, remixes, abilities, and Quick Kick, however they can float freely at slow speeds. Dying while in ghost form fully kills the user, requiring them to go through the respawn process as normal. When Reviving ends, the user is brought back to life with max health, exiting the ghost form and regaining access to their loadout, additionally resetting cooldowns of both weapons and abilities. There is no limit to how many times the user can activate Ghostwalker's effects.
perks.tips:
- Entering ghost form does not get rid of the user's summons.
- Summoner based weapons such as Zombie Staff and Summoner's Codex can use this effect as a "last stand" option, also taking advantage of an enemy's lowered guard.
- Entering ghost form does not grant the enemy player who "killed" the user any on-kill effects.
- This works well against Katana or Swiftcast which both rely on securing kills.
perks.trivia: - The user's initial death ragdoll is affected when dying again in ghost form.

statusEffects.name: Crowned
sources: Appears when teams have a difference of 8 or more points for more than 40 seconds. Given to an active player on the winning team with the most kills, healing, or mitigation, with 250 points of healing or mitigation equating to a kill. Only 1 player can be crowned at a time, and appears in Deathmatch, Team Deathmatch, King of the Hill, Subspace Takeover, and Subspace Transport, alongside their tri-teams variants.
statusEffects.description:
When receiving Crowned, the affected player gains invincibility for 1.5 seconds and 800 overhealth which decays over 8 seconds. (Similar to Divine Veil)
The affected player is permanently highlighted and the Ghostwalker perk is disabled for the duration. The affected player will be considered as in-combat and cannot respawn via the Roblox menu as long as they have this effect.

When the affected player dies, the following effects happen:
- Grants +66% remix charge to the enemy teams that killed the affected player.
- Grants points depending on the gamemode to the team or player that killed the affected player.
- Grants 4 points in deathmatch.
- Grants 7 points in team based gamemodes.
- Extends the round timer by 20 seconds if there is more than 1 minute left.

Equipping both ability slots with movement/verticality abilities also penalizes the Remix Ability reward granted from killing Crowned players.

lines: The following effects will no longer be affected by [Perk] Susceptible or [Perk] Impervious: Enlarged

Enlarged is powerful on its own, but Transmorph Ray's duration is lightyears ahead of any other remix ability. This should allow it to fall in line and prevent it from feeling oppressive, especially in times where entire teams would plan Transmorph Ray stacking ahead of time.
[Remix Ability] Transmorph Ray's Enlarged buff damage reduction has been reduced from -70% to -50%

Map Introduction Dialogue

Blue | Welcome to Bloxburg! ...Not New Bloxburg!

Red | We're really close to the one and only ROBLOX HQ so security here is at an all-time high. Watch yourselves out here.

Red | Don't cause too much trouble, everyone. This town is on maximum security after the recent event.

Blue | Can't arrest us if we take them out first! Go, go go go! Destroy, destroy!

Red | DON'T LISTEN TO BLUE. Just stay away from them if you can.

Blue | Look, Red! I can see the ROBLOX HQ from here!

Red | That's right. We're right nearby, if you'd like to check it out later.

Blue | After the game! Oh, and watch out for the cops, everyone! We didn't exactly register this place yet...

Red | 'We'? Blue, I told you to--

Red | Welcome to Builder's Bedroom, everyone. Hope the builds are something nice to look at.

Blue | These final builds are conserved and maintained after the place closed down waaaay back! Any way you can get my old stuff out, Red?

Red | Nope. That's all long gone. It's good to appreciate what we've still got here, thought.

Blue | It's a little sad this place never opened back up. I could've showed you my builds that I made way back in the day!

Red | Atleast the final few builds were maintained. It's practically just a museum now.

Blue | Let's see... lots of cover.... climbable rooftops... Yup! This is a good place to fight!

maps.name: Kin
maps.description:
Map Introduction Dialogue

Red | You ever look back on fond memories of this place?

Blue | I went to school here! I really doubt they'll still be hosting the reunion nowadays though.

Red | Maybe when this whole thing blows over, I'll contact them for you.

Red | Kin's a little crazy, but I think you'll all be fine.

Blue | Keep an eye on the storm! It's very, VERY radioactive!

Red | Watch out for the undead asweell. Some little cold got out and suddenly it was a whole 'catastrophic event,' or something. It really wasn't even that big of a deal, honestly.

Blue | Welcome to Kin, everyone! Looks like the storm hasn't dissipated yet!

Red | This place used to be a big bustling town, but there was a small cold that got blown out of proportion. Try not to breathe too much and catch it, okay?

Trivia

Developer Intro from the Patch Note [01.03.2024]

Abandoned due to a slightly contagious pathogen, we return back to one of the main cities, Kin! Beware that the residents aren't as friendly as your normal robloxian, and it's rumored that some people exposed to the area never die once. Who knows if it's true, though.

Extra Map shots

+Hidden text, found in a normally innaccessible part of the map
It's identical to the text found in "Apocalypse Rising" roblox place

One simple man is all it took
I write my story now, in this nook
His family followed in his step
The virus slowly and painfully crept
He became the dreaded Patient Zero
It was clear to me he was no hero
The virus spread slowly at first
We learned it had an insatiable thirst
One of my friends became infected
He was indeed poorly protected
The virus quickly became widespread
I LIKE BREAD
Oh how my mind is starting to go
I can feel myself becoming a foe
I carry the disease inside me now
I will not infect others, this I vow
Militaries came to destroy the infected
But what they saw was unexpected
The civilians now all gone
And the streets that they came upon
Were full and bursting with the infected
But alas, they were not unaffected
They ran like the others
To the MrFields for cover
I can feel my mind mind slipping away faster
This will certainly be a disaster
I wrote what I know, hoping for someone finds this
If you do see this resist, resist, resist
Resist the infected
DO NOT BE DETECTED
THERE WILL BE NO HELP

maps.name: Plates of Faith
maps.description:
Random events

Extra platforms

Random blocks of various colors and translucency appear all over the map. They can obstruct passages, allow for some unusual juking and provide unexpected cover.
Sometimes "extra platforms" can be just a few outsteretched diagonal sticks in the middle of the map.

Protective shields

Impenetrable cut spheres spawn in random spots across the map. No attack can go through it, it's not an obstruction for a player.

Bridges

Random platforms get bridged.

Rain Clouds

Purely cosmetic.

Platform Movement

Some platforms can start moving after a short warning.

Map Introduction Dialogue

Blue | This place used to be so cool and fun, but now it's just another stinky dock!

Red | It's still pretty hazardous. Watch your step, everyone. You never know if you're backing up into a hole or anything.

Red | You know, I used to work here as the game master. It's kinda fitting, seeing where I'm at now.

Blue | You worked here too?! I was a balloon boy! How come we never saw each other?

Red | I was probably too busy tormenting the players. Sounds bad, but it paid really well.

Red | Nice choice. We'll meet you all at Plates of Fate- Faith.

Blue | I kinda miss how it was back then...

Red | It was too crazy. #1 rule of Project Remix is to have fun, and that wasn't it.

Trivia

maps.description:
Map Dialogue

Introductory

Blue | ROBLOX Titanic! Red found it and restored it back to it's former glory for you all! Everyone say thank you! Thank you, Red!

Red | It's got some holes, but I'll keep an eye on the game in case there's any emergency. Good luck, everyone.

Blue | You did great! If it's stable enough to fight on, it's good enough for the game!

Red | It's not perfect and barely floats, but I'll step in if it gets too bad.

Red | Nice. We all get a free cruise.

Blue | Don't you even think about relaxing, Red! You still have a job to do!

Red | Yeah, yeah... They wouldn't have known, but sure. Rat me out.

Titanic crash during Round 2

Blue | Red? RED | LOOK OUT |

Red | Huh? Ohhh. Great.

Blue | AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAHHHHH | | |

Red | You dork.

...

Blue | HUH?!?! WHAT *IS* THAT?!?!

Red | ...That's new... I'll see if I can do anything about it. Nope.

Blue | You didn't even try!

Blue | RED, LOOK OUT | |

Red | ...

Blue | WWOOOAAAAAAAAAAAAHHHHHHHH | | | | | !

Red | Quit it, we're fine.

Blue | YOU SAID WE'D BE FINE | !

Red | Well... uh... I'm Sure it's not *that* mad.

Trivia

Pre-rework

Fixing the ship dialogue

Red | I got it, folks. Don't worry.

Blue | Thank you!

Blue | You all okay? Good! Red, some help, please?!

Red | Oh, yeah. No problem.

Blue | Red! The ship!

Red | Huh? Oh. Got it.

Blue | Red! Pay attention!

Red | I got it, I got it...

mechanics.name: Mechanics
mechanics.summary: Mechanics refer to various universal functions that build up the groundwork of Project Remix.

sections.loadout:
This section regards the player's loadout as well as other related sections

[The Armory]
Main article: Armory
The Armory is a shop accessible through the load-out menu, where several things can be bought using in-game currency. There are 8 different areas in the Armory.

The main page is where you can access all of the other areas in the armory, featuring Cami, who will make several different remarks, most notably when opening the armory, trying to buy a locker key during a round, etc.

There are 4 basic shops on the leftmost side of the shop, where you can purchase Weapons, Skins, Abilities, and Perks using Tix.

To the right of the shops, you can find Lockers and a place to edit your profile. Below your profile, you can access Requests.

[Weapon Levels]
Main article: Levels
All weapons have levels, which are used to unlock variants of the weapon, and grant you a few when you reach a new level.

You can increase your weapon levels by keeping using them in fights. Winning or losing also helps increase your weapon level, too, but winning grants more than losing.

Each weapon has a level cap of 50, and reaching this cap rewards a mastery bonus along with a blue gem-like sticker of that weapon.

[Currency]
Main article: Currency
The main currencies in Project Remix are Tix and Rebucks. With Tix being more common to obtain than Rebucks. Tix is used to buy all the weapons found in the armory as well as abilities, remixes, perks, and most skins, while Rebucks are used for buying certain legendary skins.

[Parties]

Parties allow players to group up with 1 friend, guaranteeing they will always be on each other's team during team Gamemodes. You can party with anyone in the server as long as they are not currently in a team. Partied players will be recognizable with a green outline and username. Parties with players with weapon level 150+ will be paired with fewer players during matchmaking. Parties cannot be joined if there are 6 players or fewer in the server, or while a round is ongoing. You can privately message party members by pressing tab twice while chatting.

To invite someone to your party, click the Party tab in your loadout menu, then select Invites, and invite a player. When a player is invited, they'll hear a jingle and receive a message in the killboard. To join, go to the same Invites menu, then click join on the party host's row.

[Double Equip Penalty]
Main article: Double Equip Penalty
This is a mechanic that only applies to abilities where equipping 2 certain abilities together will have it so when you use one of the abilities, the other will go on cooldown and have its cooldown time. This is done in order to prevent oppressive loadouts(an example being double timebomb thrown at the same time, being able to cause 200 damage), though this penalty is not limited to stacking the same ability.
sections.combat:
Mechanics that influence combat, be it how you approach it, or how it affects you in combat.

[Spawning]
Main article: Spawning
During a match in order to "spawn" into the map and play, the player must press space which will play a animation(which can be skipped by pressing space another time) of them jumping out of the helicopter and afterwards it give a view of the entire map, the player is able to hold m1 to spawn at their cursor. There are some restrictions on where you are able to spawn an example being unable to next to opponents, a more detailed review can be found in the main article.

[Health]
Main article: Health
Health is what determines if you are alive or defeated in Project Remix. Every Player has a base 200 Max HP, with Weapons and game mode determining your max HP when you first spawn in, either increasing it or decreasing it. There are only 2 ways to change your max HP during gameplay, with those 2 being 12 Arcana and Scarlet Aeonia.

[Natural Regeneration & Reduced Healing]

(Reduced Healing is a status effect and will be moved)
If you haven't sustained any damage in 5 seconds, you will begin to regenerate your health at a rate of 25 per second, in increments of 3. This regeneration effect ends the moment you take damage from any source. Regeneration will also happen upon getting a kill or assist.

Upon taking any damage from an enemy, you will be put in a reduced healing state, indicated by the red scratch marks on your health bar. In this state, you receive -30% healing for the next 2 seconds. This effect will not apply from self-damage.

[Damage Reduction]
When being attacked by more than 2 or more players, you will receive a 20% damage protection for __ seconds.

[Health Modifier]
In team-based game modes, the players have +25 increased max health.

[Objectives]
Main article: Gamemodes
Also see: Maps
Objectives are the main goal of each project remix match and act as a goal you must complete with your team, or by yourself. The usual goal is to get a higher score than the other team, with a current total of 8(might be more) objectives in Project Remix, currently, that being:
- Deathmatch: You fight alone and try to get the most kills by the end of the match
- Team Deathmatch: You fight with a team against another and try to get the most kills at the end of the match.
- Tri Deathmatch: teams are split into 3 and act the same as Team Deathmatch
- King of the Hill: 2 Teams fight to stay in a selected area that moves around the map. After some time, standing in the zone earns points; the highest score wins.
- Tri King of the Hill: the same as King of the Hill, but with 3 teams instead.
- Fishing For Flags: 2 teams fight for a flag in the middle of the map and attempt to bring it back to their "base"
- Subspace Takeover: 2 teams fight for a giant subspace tripmine and try to push it further than the other; this is similar to Overwatch's Push gamemode.
- Subspace Transport: 2 teams fight to either push a subspace tripmine to the end, or stop it from reaching the end. This is similar to TF2's payload gamemode.
Certain maps restrict objectives; for example, MadLab restricts objectives to only deathmatch and its variants.

[Mana & Action Points]
Main article: Mana & Action Points
Mana and Action Points are a resource meter used as a universal resource, though not all abilities or weapons make use of it. An example of a weapon that uses Action Points would be Fists

There are weapons, perks, and abilities that are able to drain action points of the target like Black Hand and Slam Dunk.

Action Points recharge by 2% per second. After 3 seconds of use, it will begin regenerating at a rate of 20% per second.

When completely drained, the bar will remain empty temporarily, then will instantly begin recharging at its swifter rate. During this state, it cannot be used until 20% of the bar is full.

[Climbing]
Main article: Movement
Climbing is an action performed when facing a wall and holding the jump key. The user will begin climbing upwards, slowing down towards the end of the duration. This mechanic uses an invisible meter and is only affected by Paint Bucket's paint passive and the perk High Climb. Climbing duration is 0.9 seconds by default, and 2.7 seconds with High Climb.
Wall hopping is a technique done by double-tapping the spacebar while climbing. Doing so will launch you from the wall, and scales with movement speed. On a successful wall hop, you lose ~0.7 seconds of climb time and 20 Action Points. By default, this tech can only be used once in the air. However, with High Climb, it can be done 3 times without touching the ground.

[Swimming]
Swimming is a mechanism that works in pairs with the environmental water. Once submerged in a deep enough body of water, the Player will begin to swim, represented by floating around waist height, with the player slowly sinking until they drown after 2 seconds. The player is able to climb out of the water or use a movement ability to get out, though the player must touch the ground in order to reset the swimming timer. (need to be checked) Being Dazed just before entering the water will cause the Player to instantly drown.

[Quick Kick]
Also see: Movement
Quick kicks are melee attacks performed by pressing V on your keyboard. They deal 30 damage and have a cooldown of 1 second. Landing a successful kick has a small knockback effect that will push you back slightly. This effect is amplified based on your current backward velocity, meaning you will be pushed back farther if you are moving backward. Using a quick kick, interrupt your weapon from attacking for about .3 seconds (confirmation needed). This is most noticeable on fast-firing weapons such as the Tommy Gun. Being airborne while quick kicking doesn't pause your movement, making it optimal to jump before kicking.

Certain weapons may alter the quick kick's abilities. Using a skateboard, your quick kick will deal 20 extra damage and push you back significantly farther. Using a minigun, your quick kick will knock enemy players away.

Quick kicks are available on any weapon, at any time, aside from states that restrict abilities, such as Scarlet Aeonia's animation. They can be useful for dealing some extra damage to opponents in melee range, using the knockback effect to distance yourself from an enemy, or finishing an opponent off while reloading.

[Movement Disruption]
Main article: Knockback
There's a handful of weapons, abilities, and remixes that are able to disrupt a player's movement, which would include pulling, pushing, slowing, tripping, and more. These are used in order to position the other player to your advantage, whether to back them away or to set up for a combo. The target player's size also determines the amount of movement disruption they will get, as players who have an increase in size will get knocked back further than those with a smaller size.

[Global Speed Cap]
See also: Movement
Every player is limited to up to +80% increased movement speed (36 studs per second). Epicsauce's Inferno effect bypasses this, alongside Sprint by +80% and Prayer of Speed by +40% for melee weapons.

[Remix Charge]
Main article: Remixes

Each remix has its own cost of points, depending on its category. Remixes charge passively and slowly, but you can deal damage or support your team to make the charging faster.

The charge will turn from orange-red to blue if the point requirements are met.

The charge does not get reset if you KO-ed.

By default, remix charge will be refunded if the Player dies 1.5 seconds after activating their remix, certain remixes have this period shortened.

[Remix Charge Multiplier]
This is a mechanic that affects how fast or slow a remix charges. All players have a passive remix charge of 20 points per second; this changes to 10 points per second if the player is on the winning team, as it has a higher score than the other team(though I don't know how it determines who is winning or losing in subspace transport). Certain game modes can change the rate at which remixes are charged. Subspace game modes have a -30% penalty on remix charge in general(assuming both passive and direct charge gained).

There is also a global Remix ability cost multiplier that is in place which increases the amount of points needed for a remix up to +35% dependent on the amount of players there are the more players, the higher the multiplier.(the scale for this is unknown)

[Kills & Assists]
If you land the final strike on any enemy, you will be granted a kill. If you've dealt at least 50 damage to an opponent and another player finishes them off, you will still be granted a kill in the form of an assist. Kills can be viewed on the player list for each round, and every kill you've ever gotten will count towards your Lifetime Kills, including assists (confirmation needed).

[Status Effects]
Main article: Status Effects
Status effects are a mechanic that can be induced in several ways, either by weapons, abilities, gamemode, or map. All status effects are removed on death and usually have a set time before they are removed, with some exceptions. For most status effects, if you are affected by it, it will show up in the middle of the screen with a bar showing how long it lasts. Though there are some effects that do not show up, such as bleed.

[Communication Wheel(Needs to be redone)]

The communication wheel can be accessed by holding C and has four options to choose from. The "Hello!" and "Thanks!" options change voices depending on your voice pack selected, and have a few different voice lines per option. All available communications options include:

- Emote: Chooses from a random emote that is equipped in the Armory. Each emote plays music and emits particles
- "Hello!": Plays a "Hello!" voice based on your voice pack, and displays a wave sticker
- Deploy Flag: Places a flag that shows your current image ID for the kill flag
- "Thanks!": Plays a "Thanks!" voice based on your current voice pack, and displays a thumbs-up sticker

[Remix Ability Cost Multiplier]
Global Remix Ability cost multiplier is +60% (increased from +40% on 2026-11-13).

[Voice Line Communication]
Voice line communication (Hello and Thanks, excluding pings) has an adaptive cooldown starting at 0.002s, doubling for each line within 10s up to a 1.5s cap (2026-11-12).
sections.environment:
[Map Events/Hazards]
Main article: Map Events
Map events are a unique event that happens on a specific map, be it a constant obstacle that the player must avoid or a temporary change.

An example is a flash Flood is an event that happens naturally on Raving Raceway. During these events, the water level rises quickly (though this is different from the map water hazard), and all players receive lower gravity while in the water. This does not affect fire-based effects or weapons. On Raving Raceway, the water will rise to its peak immediately, then stay that way for a minute before lowering back down.

[Map Elements]
Elements in maps that have a constant presence in most maps, either to benefit the player or to their detriment.
[Health Packs]
Health Packs are scattered around on every map, and there are two variants. The first one is a small health pack, usually in places you are more often to fight, while large health packs are usually in secluded areas you have to retreat to. Small health packs heal for 100, while large health packs heal for 300 (confirmation needed). Small health packs respawn after 10 seconds, and large health packs respawn after 30 seconds. All health packs remove negative status effects and heal for over 1 second.

[Jump Pads]
Jump Pads are placed on every map to allow quick vertical travel to higher spots on the map. The velocity they provide is predetermined, and each player has a 5-second cooldown. When you step on a Jump Pad, you create a green particle effect, similar to that of a Super Jump or Hop.

[Water]
Water is a map hazard that appears in certain maps, causing players to start swimming once submerged.

[Weather]
Every map switch, the weather is randomized from 5 major selections:

- Sunset / Sunrise
- Midday
- Night
- Cloudy, no rain
- Cloudy rain

There are variations of each, such as clouds and sun position being in different places.

Some map-specific weather conditions are set and are always the same for these maps:

- Mad Tech Factory - Green fog
- Kin - Slight green fog
- Builder's Bedroom - Mid Day
sections.experimental mechanics:
Also see: Removed and Scrapped Content
This section covers current mechanics that are defined as experimental and may or may not stay in the game. If the mechanics become official, they will be moved into their respective categories.

[Map Destruction]
Main article: Map Destruction

Map destruction is an experimental mechanic that allows certain weapons, abilities and remixes to destroy the map, creating new openings and opportunities for the player. Map destruction is voxel based, meaning that destruction will cause the object to break up into cube shapes. There are certain object that are unable to be destroyed, some include the floor for most maps, Roblox's terrain.

mechanics.name: "Thanks!" Mechanics
mechanics.summary: Slingshot's "Thanks!" technique is unique in its ability to turn its enemies' projectiles back against them. Though the general idea is straight forward, there are a few mechanics that require explanation (especially because the in game description is currently outdated).

sections.\"thanks!\":
By holding Secondary Fire, the user enters third person and swings a net in front of them. Doing so drains Mana, collects nearby enemy projectiles in a 14 stud radius, and grants 40% damage resistance while active. Projectile storage has a capacity of 40; most projectiles take up 1 ammo slot and all projectiles are doubled upon collection (except those fired by another "Thanks!" user). Some projectiles use more (up to 4) or less (down to 1/12) space.
[Firing]
Stored projectiles will be fired instead of pellets at the normal fire rate when using Primary Fire. They are released in first-in-first-out order, meaning the first projectile caught is the first to be fired. Projectiles are fired simultaneously in groups of up to 3 ammo, and larger (4) projectiles are fired individually. For example:
- If three bullets (1) are stored, they will be fired together
- If three Astel shots (1/4), two bullets (1), and two pellets (1) are stored, the Astel and bullets will be fired first, followed by the pellets
- If two bullets (1) and one Hyperlaser shot (4) are stored, the bullets will be fired first, followed by the Hyperlaser shot.

Some bullet-type projectiles become Stray Bullets, which are 25 damage hitscan projectiles. mechanics.name: Crowned
mechanics.summary: Crowned is a match mechanic, allowing losing teams or players to catch up by killing the winning team's best performing player.

sections.overview:
In order for Crowned to appear, teams or players must have an 8 or more point difference for more than 40 seconds during the match. When fulfilled, an active player on the winning team with the most kills, healing, or mitigation is granted Crowned. Players cannot be given Crowned twice in a row.

When granted, the affected player gains invincibility for 1.5 seconds and gains 800 overhealth which decays over 8 seconds. (Similar to Divine Veil) While crowned, the player is highlighted and the perk Ghostwalker is disabled. When the crowned player dies, the teams or player that killed the crowned player gains +66% remix ability charge and points depending on the gamemode, 4 in Deathmatch and 7 in Team Deathmatch or King of the Hill. Additionally, if there is more than 1 minute left in the round, it will extend the timer by 20 more seconds.

Crowned will be removed when the user's team loses the lead, upon entering overtime, or when team rebalancing occurs. It is present in all gamemodes except Fishin' For Flags.

Note: Equipping both ability slots with Movement/Verticality abilities also penalizes the Remix Ability charge reward from killing Crowned players.

mechanics.name: Damage Resistance
mechanics.summary: Damage Resistance is a player stat which determines how much damage they receive from attacks.

sections.overview: Damage resistance stacks multiplicatively. For example, a player with Body: Large (+15%) affected by Protection (+60%) would have 64% damage resistance.

mechanics.name: Death
mechanics.summary: Death is a player event in Project Remix, which occurs when someone's Health reaches zero.

sections.points:
A death usually results in points lost or gained towards an objective. In King of The Hill, for example, dying while outside of the zone subtracts 2 points for your team.

When a player with the Crowned status dies, the player or team responsible is rewarded with the appropriate amount of points depending on the gamemode; 4 in Deathmatch and 7 in Team Deathmatch or King of the Hill.
sections.charge refunding: There exists a brief window between activating any Remix ability and dying, where the player will be refunded the full build cost of the remix. The timing may vary depending on the player's weapon.
sections.sounds:
When a player dies, a random sound effect is played. The sounds are usually brief snippets of audio from memes or other games such as:
- The Wilhelm scream
- Heavy from Team Fortress 2
- Youtube: What a Magnificent Pair of Bananas

mechanics.name: Double Equip Penalty
mechanics.summary: Double Equip Penalty is a feature limited to abilities where equipping certain abilities together will cause a penalty, where using one of your abilities will put the other one on cooldown for half of its max duration. Abilities with multiple charges will consume both charges. Still, if the ability is already on a cooldown, it will only consume the current ability being used while resetting the cooldown of the other ability to half.

Abilities with multiple charges will consume both charges. Still, if the ability is already on a cooldown, it will only consume the current ability being used while resetting the cooldown of the other ability to half.

It will be listed out in the order they appear, and duplicates will be counted (example: timebomb and starfrag, and starfrag and timebomb).

Last updated: 12/21/2025

The Remix Ability buildup penalty from equipping both ability slots with movement/verticality abilities also penalizes the Remix Ability reward granted from killing Crowned players (2026-11-13).

[Movement/Verticality Remix Charge Modifier]
Equipping 0 Movement/Verticality abilities grants +25% Remix Ability charge gain, 1 grants 0%, and 2 inflicts -25% (Ravenous Maul and Rejuvenating Dash also count as Movement abilities for this modifier). Having both slots equipped as Movement/Verticality also penalizes the Remix Ability reward from killing Crowned players.

mechanics.name: Health
mechanics.summary:
Health is a core gameplay mechanic that determines the amount of damage the player or a construct can take before dying. Likewise, healing is the act of restoring health.

The player's max health depends on the weapon they are using, as some grant different health bonuses or penalties. The base maximum health is 225, and 200 during Deathmatch.

sections.healing:
After not taking any damage for 5 seconds or getting a kill/assist, the player naturally regenerates health at a rate of 25 health per second, in increments of 3. Taking damage while regenerating ends this effect.

Some status effects, such as Heal Boost and Regen can increase this amount.

[Health Packs]
Health Packs can be found on every map and gives health when picked up. There are small and large health packs, which heal for 100 and 250 respectively. Small health packs respawn after 10 seconds, while large packs respawn after 30 seconds. All health packs remove negative status effects and heal for over 1 second.

[Reduced Healing]
Taking direct damage from an enemy or Poison applies reduced healing, indicated by the red scratch marks on the health bar. While under the effects of reduced healing, the player receives -60% healing from all sources for 1.25 seconds. Reduced healing is not applied when taking self-damage or from most damage overtime status effects.
- The duration of reduced healing is affected by Susceptible and Impervious.

[Healing Output Penalty]
A healing penalty is applied when there are at least 2 players using a support weapon in a 120 stud radius. The healing output for each player in the radius is reduced by 17.5%.
sections.overhealth:
Overhealth is indicated by green in the player's health bar and is always depleted first when they take damage. Points of Overhealth that are removed count as a mitigation contribution for allies that applied the effect.
- In servers with less than 16 players, spawning on an ally grants them and the player +25 overhealth.
- Overhealth is unaffected by damage reduction effects such as ones granted by Body: Large and Assassin's Gambit, but with the exception of Prayer: Defense.

mechanics.summary: Hitscan is damage that is instantly dealt to targets in a path. In Project Remix, most hitscan based weapons have a short delay in their firing.

Knockback is a rare mechanic where players or enemies receive a force that pushes in them in a direction, usually in the opposite direction of an attack.

Knockback varies with each source, having different force and angles in which it is applied. Typically, the velocity is added on to the user's current velocity, however an exception to this is Javelin Throw which applies the target's velocity into a set amount.

mechanics.name: Mana & Action Points
mechanics.summary:
Mana & Action Points (AP) are gameplay mechanics in Project Remix. They are universal resources used by several weapons, abilities, and remixes.

Mana is mainly used for magic-based actions, while Action Points is reserved for physical actions. Fully depleting a meter will prevent the player from performing those actions for 4 seconds, even if the user has sufficient resources. Both resources hold 100 of their respective points and regenerates 20 points per second after 3 seconds of not being used. The rates at which AP and Mana are consumed varies depending on the action performed or weapon used.

mechanics.name: Map Events
mechanics.summary: There are specific events tied to certain maps, each of which can be uniquely beneficial, neutral, or harmful to the players. Events can range from a temporary barrier, or a constant threat to the player, being varied to the gameplay and adding another way of engaging during the game.

sections.overview: There are specific events tied to certain maps, each of which can be uniquely beneficial, neutral, or harmful to the players. Events can range from a temporary barrier, or a constant threat to the player, being varied to the gameplay and adding another way of engaging during the game.
sections.flash flood: This event is tied to Raving Raceway (and Titanic before it was replaced), where, once per match, the water level rises until it is just above the flag at the racing tower. This will stay for __ seconds before the water level sinks back down to its original height. During this time, players will have their gravity reduced while in the flood, which will cause players to jump higher and fall more slowly.
sections.storm: This event is tied to Kin, the storm is a constant event that persist throughout the match. It is a red border that slowly moves around the map, and is a way to stop players from spreading out too far, as going past the barrier and staying in the storm for 3 seconds will cause the player to take damage 25 damage every __ seconds with the damage compounding(25, 50, 75, etc. needs to be checked), along with the player's screen being given a red tint and all sounds becoming muffled. Only the player's camera is being accounted for when seeing if the player is in the storm, so players in third person can either have their player in the storm without being affected by it by facing the storm, or be outside the storm, but still be affected by the storm if they are close to the border and is facing away from it.
sections.titanic crash:
An event in Titanic

During the second round in Titanic after __ seconds a cutscene will play, this will disable all player's movement and zooming out to show the Titanic crashing into an iceberg causing the screen to go white and KO-ing all players on the map. After the cutscene end the map will transition into the crashed variant, this only happens once.
sections.portals: A constant event in Sunken Heights, and The Grand College
sections.spikes: A constant hazard in Builder's Bedroom
sections.acid: A constant hazard in Haunted Mansion
sections.plate events: A constant hazard in Plates of Faith
sections.explosive barrels: A hazard in Mad Tech Factory

mechanics.name: Movement
mechanics.summary:
This page covers movement in Project Remix, which can range from universal actions to actions only tied to certain weapons, abilities, or perks.

As a baseline, the default movement speed is 20 studs/s. Increased or decreased movement speed is multiplicative to the base speed.

sections.controls: Players control themselves using movement keys (W A S, and D). Pressing the jump key (Space) makes the player jump. Holding jump next to a wall allows them to climb it.
sections.bunnyhopping:
Bunnyhopping (also bhopping) is universal technique that allows the player to move much faster along the ground.

Bunnyhopping is a technique found in many games that involves repeatedly jumping to preserve momentum and increase acceleration, usually dependent on strafe jumping. However, Project Remix does not have traditional bunnyhopping. Instead, jumping itself provides the player a small burst of speed, allowing the player to jump soon after they hit the ground to preserve this momentum and further increase their speed up to +50%. Bunnyhopping is available to every player no matter their loadout, making it a simple way to move faster without abilities.
sections.climbing:
Climbing allows the player to scale vertical surfaces and is performed by holding the jump button while facing a vertical surface. It is not required to hold any other movement key. Climbing speed is 22 studs/s, and climbing duration is 0.9 seconds. About halfway through the duration, climb speed begins decaying to 0 studs/s. By default, the player can climb 15 studs, and the climb duration resets when the player stands on solid ground.

At the end of the duration, or by releasing and then pressing jump at any time while climbing, the player performs a wall jump, consuming up to 20 Action Points while boosting themselves off the wall. If the player holds forward while jumping, this jump is instead directed upwards. Combined with jumping before climbing, this allows the player to scale walls up to ~25 studs high. Wall jumping will set the climbing duration to 0, preventing the player from climbing until they touch the ground.

[High Climb]
With the perk High Climb, climbing speed is increased by 50% to 33 studs/s and climbing duration is tripled to 2.7 seconds. This allows the player to climb 62 studs, up to ~70 studs if jumping before and after climbing. Jumping while climbing subtracts ~0.7 seconds of climbing duration.
sections.hop preservation:
Abilities used:
- Hop
Weapons used:
- Laser Scythe Energy Whirl
When using Hop or Energy Whirl's m2 while in the air, it allows you to preserve your current momentum as well as redirect it.
sections.dash preservation:

- Dash I
- Dash II
Weapons used:
- Katana (all variants)
- Linked Sword
- Paladin's Oath
When using the shown weapon's secondary ability after, use dash ability ( timing varies between weapons and variant) in order to preserve the momentum.

mechanics.summary: Projectiles are emitted entities that travel at a certain speed. Unlike hitscans, projectiles requires time to travel, defined by their projectile speed which differs depending on what they were fired from. Projectiles typically deal damage on contact, however some may deal healing, generate area of effects or inflict status effects on contact, with none being exclusive to each other.

mechanics.name: Spawning
mechanics.summary: Spawning is a game mechanic where the player can choose the position they wish to be placed on upon entering the map.

sections.overview:
In the loadout menu, pressing SPACE plays a quick animation where the player jumps out of the helicopter. (The user can press SPACE again mid animation to skip it) After the animation, the player enters a free-falling screen over the map, with their character doing a variety of poses as the camera shakes and zooms back and forth.

While in the free-fall screen, pressing SPACE brings up the loadout menu again without the helicopter.

Allies will have a blue radius around them, allowing other allies to spawn within it. Enemy players or certain objective points have a red radius around them, preventing players from spawning directly next to them.

Hovering over a valid surface on the map brings up a marker signaling that it is a valid place to land. Other players on your team can see the marker as well, allowing for coordination.

Holding the left click on a valid location plays a quick animation zooming into the spot as the screen turns white. (Can be disabled in settings via Gameplay > Spawning Flash Transition) After the animation finishes, the player will land in their chosen spot. Additionally, the spawn animation can be canceled by letting go early.

After spawning in, the player receives 1.5 seconds of immortality.

[Spawning on Allies]
While choosing where to spawn, there will be an icon to pick that's on a teammate as long as they are not inside an objective bubble, and the player is able to click and hold to spawn on them. While spawning on the icon, the player will have an increased spawning time(__ seconds), and when spawned, will have decreased invincibility and a movement debuff for one second while spawning in.

[Respawning]
When the player dies, they must wait 5 seconds before being able to spawn back in.

mechanics.name: Terrain Destruction
mechanics.summary:
Terrain Destruction is an experimental mechanic which was introduced on December 9, 2025 during a Fun Zone session. It was fully introduced to the game on December 12, 2025.

Terrain Destruction allows players to destroy many aspects of the map, including props, buildings, and artificial grounds. The only exceptions are the boundary walls and the base plate of the map.

After destruction, parts of the object fully regenerate after 15 seconds. If a player is inside while it is meant to regenerate, it is delayed by 4 seconds to give them time to escape. If they do not exit by then they are killed instantly, with a death message "Player merged with a wall." Players are able to collide on objects that are delayed when they exit it.

A list of items that are capable of terrain destruction can be found here.

mechanics.name: Constructs
mechanics.summary: Constructs are a function of Project Remix. They're everything that has a health pool meaning they can be damaged but cannot be healed. (Summoner's Codex being the exception) They can be separated into Humanoid and Non-Humanoid. Humanoids Constructs will grant on-kill benefit as if the player killed another player. These include the healing, kickstarting regeneration, and resetting cooldowns. (The perk Swiftcast does not reset ability cooldowns upon a Humanoid Construct kill.)

This is not inclusive of /votekick or /changelogs, as they can be used anywhere.

misc.name: Fun Zone
misc.summary:

Fun Zones are developer-hosted events which often introduce new content to Project Remix which aren't ready to be introduced in public lobbies.

They are only accessible by joining the (HM) Discord. When one is hosted, a link to a fun zone private server will be sent inside the #pr-sneak-peaks channel. After it has ended, the link will be deleted, alongside everything relevant to it.

misc.name: Music Bands
misc.summary:
There is a number of Music Bands that have contract with Project Remix for streaming.

Red & Blue

Both are the faces and the main band for Project Remix. So far, they have the most songs present in PR.

+Releases
Crossroads Chaos | Red & Blue make their first debut as Project Remix's hosts! No Robloxian would've expected the project's complete & utter rise to fame...

Fjurious Fjords | Red makes a new instrumental sampling an old tracks he found on his laptop. Blue is completely on board. Enjoy the music, contestants!

Twisted Plastic | Red turns up the heat with some adrenaline-fueling beats. Blue's here to hype it up. Go win the game!

Crossroads Chaos (★ Edition) | Red & Blue reminisce on their first debut track and decides it's time to spice things up a bit.

C.A.LLING C.A.RD | When things seem grim in life, Red & Blue implore you to come in contact & get with the project. You know what to do.

Trivia

T0M0

An extremely popular robotic Pop-Star.

+Releases
V1RTUAL.C0NNECTION | Who could resist a brand deal with Robloxia's biggest popstar? It's said that Blue's heart fully stopped when Red announced he managed to get everything signed. T0M0's here to bring her love and joy to the games. Will you join and be her next biggest fan?

else if i | All of Robloxia is dancing along to the newest hit of everyone's favorite popstar! Her lyrics inspire Robloxians all across the world, but her latest song seems to be letting out her true inner feelings.

callback | T0M0 returns from her hiatus to bring us a nostalgic hit for many fans - a remaster of her debut single, 'callback'! "I want all of my fans to know that I love you so very much, and what better way to show it than to remind everyone of our first memory together!"

iNLETS

A garage band of rogue Dummies brought to Project Remix by a Mysterious Woman in Orange.

+Releases
iNTERTWINE | [ iNLETS ARE THE NEXT BEST THING. CANNOT COMPARE. ]
Red's not one to normally cut deals easily but according to Blue, iNLETS, a small band based in a tiny garage seemed to join in on the project rather quickly after a... "weirdo woman in orange" (...?) had a private meetup with Red.

i_ii_iii_iV | [ WE HEAR YOU. YOU HEAR US. WE HAVE ORDER. LET US SHOW YOU. ]
iNLETS are back(?) with another intrusive track. Red doesn't look very happy, but Blue loves dancing to the beat.

iMPASSE | iNLETS are back with an official declaration of war to all of humanity. ...Or is it just another single? Red & Blue won't make an official statement about it.

iNTEGRATION | "[ WE HEARD YOU'RE OPENING UP A MUSIC STORE. iNTEGRATE US. ]"

The group was then quickly escorted away from the subway. Always keep your phone on hand in case of emergencies!

Midnight Mercy

"Reformed" Midnight Motors.

+Releases
Hangout ‘Til We Breakout | Midnight Mercy (formerly Midnight Motors) are back in business and ready to rock! Thanks to their new member for bailing them out, they're sure to give everyone the time of their life. Well, not like they have a choice. Joining Project Remix is probably the best pick when serving parole.

7th Sanctum

+Releases
Not Now, Not Ever! | 7th Sanctum is a known record label for many bands Blue's older works, but he never expected his old publisher to come on board with the project.

- "I was fine when T0M0 came around, I never questioned when that weirdo woman went into your office, why did you let him sign up after everything I told you about him?! You KNOW how how annoying he is!"

- "Listen, at this point, we're in too deep. It's good publicity. I know how you feel, but even you should know how our audience would react if we turned him down."

Cherry Bomb! | "Absolutely not! No way! Nada! No, no, NO!"

"Letting him set up shop there is gonna put us on the map. I thought you said you wanted to be famous, Blue."

"But that's where I head for my coffee run | You're gonna ruin that spot for me?!"

"As if you need coffee in the first place. Come on, let's get to it."

マテオ

The name reads as "Mateo".

+Releases
1.UNDEAD.1 | An (alleged) fellow Project Remix staff proposes Red & Blue implement their 'beats' into the playlist, giving a mysterious call at the dead of night.

- "Tell them my BloxCloud, bro... I make music, bro... Get them to listen, bro... I need followers, bro..."

- "Can you tell us your name?"

- "Nah, bro... I'm like, an anonymous artist, bro... A lone wolf, bro... Don't mess with me, bro..."

- "[REDACTED], you don't even try to hide your voice!"

(4:32 AM. The applicant continued to choose to remain anonymous.)

updates.author: meal(HM) Team
updates.content:
@project-remix-updates the last update was pretty rough for melee users so this update should change the game up to be more rewarding for everyone aswell as update some older, outdated, and boring weapons


== Balancing ==

Minigun
Rounds increased from 200 to 300

Movement speed reduction while firing reduced from 45% to 65%

Basic Abilities are now disabled while firing

There wasn't enough trade-off in having all that damage and all that health, so this should give other players a better chance of survival while they take down minigun users.

Paintball Gun
Bullet speed increased from 1200 to 2400

New passive : Hitting enemies will reveal them to you for 5 seconds. Critical hits daze enemies for 0.8 seconds

The Paintball Gun was the first weapon ever added and ever since has been completely and utterly boring. This should allow some skill expression and give it a more unique advantage over other weapons.

Linked Sword Rework
Base damage decreased from 60 to 35

Secondary damage decreased from 110 to 50

Lunge speed decreased from 200 to 120

Passive removed : Heal for 50% of sword damage dealt

Passive added : Deal 300% lunge damage to targets under 50% health

Linked sword was always lackluster and always felt like a worse version of the katana. This change gives the sword a more unique gimmick as a melee weapon.

Slingshot
Primary fire damage decreased from 40/50 to 35/45

Slingshot had a way higher kill time with a higher fire rate compared to other weapons. This brings it down a tiny bit just to alleviate that huge amount of damage.

Katana
Passive is now compatible with other bleed-related weapons such as Bladed Tutu and Crimson Katana.

With the Remix Ability passives update, some passives weren't updated to be consistent with other weapons. This change should add more combo potential for the katana's unique passive.

E.T.Death
Firing cooldown increased from 0.15 to 0.2

Damage decreased from 35/70 to 30/40

Fire rate was way too high and the damage was way too inconsistent. This should make it a more balanced AND more reliable weapon.

Kill passive for everyone
Getting a kill will now restores 50% of max health

This should make kills more rewarding for all players aswell as make melee users rely less on self-heal buffs.

updates.content:
==== Bugfixes ====

Fixed an issue that would loop spawn a bunch of dropped weapons if the player weapon swapped too quickly

Fixed an issue where Magician's Tophat, Bladed Tutu, Black Hole Bomb, Darkheart, and Epicsauce couldn't hit constructs

Fixed an issue that made the spawning camera stuck if the round ended while spawning

Fixed an issue where damage/healing over time values would be inaccurate

Fixed an issue that allowed Healing Tether players to latch onto each other

Hyperlaser Gun no longer phases through forcefields

Fixed thick projectiles phasing through walls

Fixed an issue that allowed weapons to de-level

 ==== Balancing == ==

RangedDual Rocket Launcher melee impact damage has been reduced from 55 to 45

 Skateboard range has been decreased from 10 to 8 studs

Skateboard damage has been increased from 20 to 25

 Grenade Launcher projectile size has been increased from 0.4 to 0.65

Adjusted Grenade Launcher aiming direction

 AbilitiesGrappling Hook latch distance has been increased from 1.5 to 3 studs

Trowel wall health has been reduced from 350 to 300

Barrier Pearl can no longer push and collide with enemies

 Weapon LevelsEXP earned from healing has been doubled

EXP earned from dealing damage has been doubled

EXP from getting a kill has been increased from 25 to 75

 GamemodesPoints stolen from stealing a Capture Point has been reduced from 75 to 50

 ==== Changes ====

Added a silly Ragdoll Death Force slider in Gameplay settings

 Assists now function in all gamemodes

Kill assists now grant kill effects and kill regen

Kill regen can no longer be cancelled within 1 second of recieving the buff

 Bubble Barrier and other constructs can now block Remote Airstrike

Bubble Barrier and other constructs can now block Subspace Tripmines

 Lockout can now cancel Healing Tether

Fall damage is no longer inflicted if the damage was under 25

 Players' teams are now visible in the chat

You can no longer dance while a round is active

Winning EXP is no longer rewarded if you had less than 5 kills and if you dealt less than 600 healing

Required EXP for levels over 50 have been doubled (if you are over level 50, you may lose a level or two but your accumulated EXP remains the same!)

 Overhealth has been reprogrammed and will now be more responsive

Giving overhealth will now count as HEALING DEALT and will also give Remix Ability charge

 Damage towards constructs no longer count toward your DAMAGE DEALT stat

Constructs are now able to recieve damage over time

 Burst Rifle crosshair visual spread has been reduced by 50%

 ==== Map Changes ====

The health pack distribution and density have been adjusted in the following maps :

Shipping Docks Crossroads Haunted Mansion Plates of Faith Raving Raceway The Heights ROBLOX Titanic  The Capture Zone distribution and density have been adjusted in the following maps :

Shipping Docks Crossroads Haunted Mansion Plates of Faith Raving Raceway  ROBLOX Titanic now has no-stand colliders on top of the tall steam thingies

Plates of Faith bridges now only last for up to 30 seconds

Slightly optimized Shipping Docks further

Added new jump pads in Shipping Docks

 Raving Raceway now has a new map event!

ROBLOX Titanic now has a new map event!

 ==== Weapon Reworks ====

Laser Finger Pointers!

Deal a starting 30 damage/healing/push per second, maxing at 100 at 100% charge  Primary Fire to deal damage Middle mouse to push enemies Secondary fire to heal allies Charge up laser power by dealing laser damage Heal for 50% of inflicted laser damage  Shotgun!

+25 max health +25% increased move speed Hold down Secondary Fire to charge forward A powered charge dazes opponents for 1 second  Superball!

Hold secondary fire to charge up a throw Superball charged hits daze enemies for 1.2 seconds
